Despite its global presence, Spotify faces challenges including a lack of content from major Korean artists due to an unconfirmed deal with Kakao M, and increasing competition from both established local players bolstering their services and new contenders like Clubhouse. The company hopes to succeed by offering tailored playlists, a vast catalog, and launching podcast services, but its success is not guaranteed in this competitive landscape.

title: BKLC Share Price & Live Chart | BNY Mellon US Large Cap Core Equity ETF
summary: The BNY Mellon US Large Cap Core Equity ETF (BKLC) offers investors exposure to US large-cap equities, tracking the S&P 500 TR USD index. The article provides live share price data, historical performance, technical analysis, and key metrics such as its current price of 140.58, a 1.2% dividend yield, and a 0.00% expense ratio. It also lists top holdings including NVIDIA, Apple, and Microsoft.

title: Can Bumble Compete?
summary: Bumble, the dating app operator, went public with its "freemium" model, but faces stiff competition from Match Group, its primary rival. Despite its focus on empowering women and a strong brand reputation, Bumble operates in a crowded market characterized by low barriers to entry and a lack of intangible assets for competitive advantage. While Bumble plans to expand into social and professional networking, it will contend with significantly larger and more established players in those markets.

title: Humana, IBM Partner To Streamline Member Engagement With AI
summary: Humana has partnered with IBM Watson Health to enhance member engagement through an AI-enabled virtual assistant. This collaboration aims to provide accurate benefits, costs, and provider information to agents, employers, and plan members, and to help members predict and reduce healthcare spending. The solution will be available to 1.3 million members in employer-sponsored medical plans and 1.8 million in dental plans, leveraging AI to improve personalization and efficiency in healthcare services.

title: Business Acronyms You Should Know: The Master Guide
summary: This master guide clarifies essential business acronyms, acting as a "Rosetta Stone" for common terms in finance, U.S. agencies, international organizations, and general business. It aims to make business news more accessible by explaining terms like IPO, M&A, S&P, CDC, EU, OPEC, GDP, ESG, and FAMGA. The article categorizes these acronyms for easy reference, helping readers navigate complex business discussions.

title: Oracle revives protest of $10B JEDI war cloud contract: Report
summary: Oracle is requesting the U.S. Supreme Court re-examine its challenge to the $10 billion Joint Enterprise Defense Infrastructure (JEDI) cloud contract, initially awarded to Microsoft in 2019. The company argues the bidding process was flawed with conflicts of interest and restricted competition. This renewed challenge comes after previous attempts by Oracle and Amazon to contest the contract award.

title: Deloitte to acquire The Working Group Inc. to enhance digital and cloud transformation
summary: Deloitte is acquiring Toronto-based digital consulting firm, The Working Group Inc. (TWG), to boost its digital and cloud transformation capabilities for mid-market and large clients. This acquisition aims to enhance Deloitte's global digital strategy and expand its offerings in product strategy, design, and engineering. TWG's team of 150 employees will integrate into Deloitte Canada's Consulting practice, strengthening its position as a leader in Canadian digital transformation.

title: News Corp signs news partnership deal with Google
summary: News Corp has finalized a global news partnership with Google, encompassing a subscription platform, advertising revenue sharing, and the development of audio and video journalism. This extensive deal concludes years of tension between Rupert Murdoch's media empire and the tech giant, especially in Australia, where Google had threatened to cease operations due to proposed content laws. The agreement follows similar deals News Corp struck with Apple and Facebook, marking a significant win for media companies seeking compensation for their premium content from large digital platforms.

title: Another success in our cloud journey
summary: UBS My Hub External, an in-house developed web app, won the Banking Technology Best use of Cloud award, highlighting UBS's successful cloud journey. The platform was instrumental in enabling 95% of the organization to work remotely during the COVID-19 pandemic, providing essential tools and reducing calls to IT helpdesks. This achievement underscores the importance of cloud computing in UBS's strategy for efficiency, agility, and client service.

title: Microsoft Starts Automatically Removing Flash From Windows
summary: Microsoft is automatically removing Adobe Flash from Windows operating systems via an update, following Adobe's official end of support and "time bomb" implementation that disabled Flash content. While this update, KB4577586, will significantly reduce Flash installations, it won't remove manually installed standalone versions, requiring users to follow Adobe's uninstallation instructions for those instances.

title: Infosys is front-runner for $1.5 billion Pfizer deal
summary: Infosys is reportedly the front-runner for a significant $1.5 billion IT outsourcing deal with Pfizer. If successful, this deal would substantially increase Infosys's total contract value for the financial year, following other major wins with Daimler and Vanguard. Both companies declined to comment on the speculation, but analysts suggest healthcare clients are investing heavily in digital transformation, cloud adoption, and new technologies.

title: What’s Changed: 2021 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Analytics and Business Intelligence Platforms
summary: Solutions Review highlights the key changes and analyses the 2021 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Analytics and Business Intelligence Platforms. The report notes increased adoption, cloud deployments, and a shift in differentiation towards augmented analytics. It details the positions of leading vendors like Microsoft, Tableau, and Qlik, alongside challengers and visionaries, while also outlining new entrants and those removed from the quadrant.

title: McDonald’s ties executive pay to diversity, releases data
summary: McDonald's has announced that 15% of executive bonuses will be tied to meeting diversity and inclusion targets. The company is also releasing demographic data on its workforce and setting specific goals to increase the representation of people of color in U.S. management and women in senior roles globally. This move comes amid increasing pressure from investors and transparency advocates for companies to address social inequality and improve diversity.

title: Exclusive: How Oracle Sells Repression in China
summary: Oracle has aggressively marketed its data analytics software to Chinese police and security forces, including those in Xinjiang, for surveillance and predictive policing, despite concerns about human rights and national security implications. This practice clashes with the company's stated values and its bid for TikTok, which aimed to prevent data access by Chinese authorities. Oracle representatives claim these were "aspirational business development ideas" and not actual implementations, but internal documents and former employees suggest otherwise.

title: SailPoint acquires Intello to increase visibility into SaaS apps
summary: SailPoint Technologies Inc. has acquired SaaS operations startup Intello Inc. for an undisclosed price to enhance visibility into SaaS applications. Intello's platform, which helps companies manage SaaS spend, usage, and compliance, will be integrated into SailPoint's Identity Platform. This acquisition aims to address the challenges of SaaS app sprawl and improve the management and security of access to these applications for businesses.

title: What is CIEM and why should CISOs care?
summary: Cloud Infrastructure Entitlement Management (CIEM) is a new category of identity-centric SaaS solutions focused on managing cloud access risk within hybrid and multi-cloud IaaS environments through administration-time controls. Unlike SIEM, CIEM uses analytics and machine learning to detect anomalies in account entitlements, such as privilege accumulation and dormant entitlements, and aims to remediate and enforce least privilege approaches. CISOs should care about CIEM because it addresses the increasing security complexities and permissions gaps in multi-cloud environments, particularly concerning inactive identities, overpermissioned active identities, cross-account access vulnerabilities, and anomalous behavior among machine identities.

title: Procurement automation enables Microsoft to outfit employee home offices
summary: During the COVID-19 pandemic, Microsoft leveraged existing procurement automation efforts and Microsoft Power Apps to quickly scale a work-from-home buying program, providing essential equipment to its 168,000 employees. The company automated the entire procurement process, from request to delivery and receipt confirmation, reducing processing time significantly and saving operational costs. This initiative showcased Microsoft's agility in supporting its workforce and built a robust system for future hybrid work models.

title: iShares S&P 500 Growth ETF Trade Ideas — AMEX:IVW
summary: This article compiles trade ideas and market sentiment analysis related to the iShares S&P 500 Growth ETF (AMEX: IVW). Several contributors discuss the ongoing debate and rotation between growth and value stocks, analyzing factors like interest rates, economic conditions, and fundamental valuations. The articles explore various market sentiment indicators over short, medium, and long terms, providing perspectives on potential market shifts and risk appetite.

title: Robotic process automation remains on a hot streak as UiPath blazes the trail
summary: The robotic process automation (RPA) market is experiencing rapid growth, fueled by the pandemic's acceleration of digital transformation initiatives. UiPath, a leading RPA vendor, recently secured $750 million in funding at a $35 billion valuation, highlighting strong investor confidence. The article explores whether this market is becoming overheated, analyzes RPA's total available market, and examines the performance of key players like UiPath, Automation Anywhere, Microsoft, Blue Prism, and Pegasystems based on ETR spending data.

title: Apple buys a company every three to four weeks
summary: Apple CEO Tim Cook revealed that the company has acquired approximately 100 companies over the past six years, averaging one acquisition every three to four weeks. These acquisitions are primarily focused on gaining technology and talent, helping Apple to integrate innovations into its products and expand into areas like AI, self-driving technology, and payments. Despite its rapid acquisition pace, Apple tends to buy smaller firms and has been more financially restrained in its purchases compared to other big tech companies.

title: Microsoft users targeted by fake FedEx and DHL emails
summary: A new phishing scam is targeting Microsoft email users with fake emails purporting to be from FedEx and DHL. These emails contain malicious links that, if clicked, lead to lookalike login pages designed to steal user credentials for Microsoft, Adobe, or work email accounts. Security researchers at Armorblox Inc. have identified at least 10,000 Microsoft email users targeted by this attack, which leverages the familiarity of delivery services to trick victims.

title: Toys Market May Set New Growth Story : Lego, Mattel, Hasbro
summary: A new report titled "The Global Toys Market Report" by HTF Market Intelligence Consulting Private Limited offers a comprehensive analysis of the global toys market for the forecast period of 2020–2026. This study provides market estimates through in-depth secondary research, primary interviews, and expert reviews, along with an outlook on current industry issues and market dynamics. It analyzes the market by type, application, major players like Lego, Mattel, and Hasbro, and geographic regions.

title: Microsoft Azure Firewall protects Microsoft’s network with Azure Firewall Manager
summary: Microsoft Digital has adopted Azure Firewall and Azure Firewall Manager to streamline managing its corporate firewalls. This shift from hardware-based to cloud-native firewall solutions, managed centrally through Azure Firewall Manager, has dramatically reduced the time and effort required to update and maintain network security across Microsoft's global operations. The move enables faster deployment of threat definitions, prevents configuration drift, and offers significant cost savings and improved agility in responding to security threats.

title: ServiceNow’s Technology May Be The Answer To Modernize Government IT
summary: ServiceNow's technology is presented as a solution for modernizing government IT, addressing the need for improved public engagement strategies and service delivery. The article highlights how ServiceNow's AI-driven ITSM solutions, including ITSM-as-a-Service on G-Cloud, can streamline communication workflows and enhance user experience for both government officials and citizens. Examples like the Tennessee Department of Human Services demonstrate tangible efficiency gains through ServiceNow's tools.

title: Qualcomm launches AR smart viewer reference design specifications
summary: Qualcomm has released its Snapdragon XR1 AR Smart Viewer reference design, aiming to guide hardware manufacturers in creating powerful and affordable AR smart glasses for consumer and enterprise use. This design utilizes the Snapdragon XR1 platform, offloading significant processing to a tethered host device to enhance performance and reduce power consumption. The reference design supports 2D app frameworks for smartphone applications in 3D environments, is compatible with Windows 10, and includes features like 6-DoF head tracking, hand tracking, and remote assistance capabilities, with contributions from partners like Microsoft, Lenovo, and Nreal.

title: Stevanato Group launches Artificial Intelligence platform to further enhance detection performance of its visual inspection machines
summary: Stevanato Group has launched an Artificial Intelligence platform, based on Deep Learning models, to enhance the detection performance of its visual inspection machines for the biopharmaceutical industry. The platform can achieve up to 99.9% defect detection accuracy, significantly reducing false rejections and improving productivity, especially for difficult-to-inspect biotech drugs. Leveraging a partnership with Microsoft Azure, the cloud-based system ensures compliance with pharmaceutical data management and security requirements while providing continuous customer support and advanced monitoring tools.

title: American Express rolls out new Digital Receipts feature
summary: American Express has launched its new Digital Receipts feature, allowing customers to easily track and identify online purchases from merchants such as Google, Microsoft, Square, and Apple. This initiative aims to enhance transparency, reduce confusion over transactions, and provide greater account protection against fraudulent charges, especially given the surge in e-commerce. The service provides detailed purchase information directly through the Amex App or website.

title: How Capital One Moved Its Data Analytics to the Cloud
summary: Capital One, a leader in technology-driven banking, successfully transitioned its data analytics from on-premise data centers to the public cloud, becoming the first U.S. bank to do so in 2020. This move leveraged the Snowflake Data Cloud to enhance scalability, support thousands of analysts, and meet stringent security and compliance requirements. The adoption of the cloud platform has enabled Capital One to improve customer experiences, control costs through consumption-based pricing, and gain real-time access to larger and more varied datasets.

title: We spoke to Jon Friedman, Corporate Vice President of Design & Research at Microsoft
summary: Jon Friedman, Corporate Vice President of Design & Research at Microsoft, discusses his passion for design, his career path, and Microsoft's approach to product development. He emphasizes design's role as a "connective tissue" driven by customer needs, integrating design, engineering, and research to create products for billions of users. Friedman also highlights the importance of the Microsoft Fluent Design System and the Fluid Framework in enabling seamless collaboration and empowering users to achieve their goals, particularly with the aid of AI.

title: Security top of mind for digital transformation projects
summary: A new ASUG and Onapsis survey reveals that security is a top concern for SAP customers undertaking S/4HANA migrations and other digital transformation projects, especially when moving to the cloud. The survey indicated that these modernization projects have not been significantly slowed by the COVID-19 pandemic. While cloud providers handle some security aspects, organizations remain responsible for data security and for addressing the unique complexities and vulnerabilities of SAP applications in a hybrid IT environment.

title: Accenture and Microsoft Collaborate to Help Accelerate U.K.’s Transition to Net-Zero Carbon Emissions
summary: Accenture and Microsoft are partnering with their joint venture, Avanade, to accelerate the U.K.'s transition to net-zero carbon emissions. They will leverage cloud, data, and AI expertise to help utility and energy companies transform the energy system and reduce the cost of decarbonizing electricity supply and demand. This initiative aims to reduce renewable generation costs, support cost-effective electrification, and efficiently match supply and demand to achieve a zero-carbon electricity system by 2025.

title: NUBURU establishes advisory board
summary: NUBURU Inc., a developer and manufacturer of high-power industrial blue lasers, has formed an advisory board to enhance its market position and customer understanding. The board comprises global experts from various industries, including battery and e-mobility, consumer electronics, and defense. NUBURU's CEO, Dr. Guy Gilliland, believes the board's insights into market trends and customer perspectives will be crucial for the company's strategic direction.

title: Clean Energy Fuels runs greener, boosts efficiency with Dynamics 365
summary: Clean Energy Fuels, a provider of renewable natural gas, has significantly improved its operational efficiency and sustainability efforts by implementing Microsoft Dynamics 365. The company uses various Dynamics 365 applications, including Remote Assist and HoloLens, to streamline operations, enhance technician training, and save on travel and training expenses. This integration helps Clean Energy achieve its mission of providing cleaner vehicle fuel while optimizing internal processes.

title: You Can Now Embed Pinterest Pins in Microsoft Word and OneNote. If You Want.
summary: Microsoft has introduced a new integration allowing users to embed Pinterest Pins directly into Word and OneNote documents through a simple cut-and-paste method. This functionality, particularly useful for OneNote and the web version of Word, aims to enhance presentations, information packs, and educational content. Microsoft notes that educators have specifically requested this feature, suggesting new branding and informative opportunities.

title: Announcing The Forrester New Wave™: Cybersecurity Risk Ratings Platforms, Q1 2021
summary: Forrester has published its New Wave™ report on Cybersecurity Risk Ratings Platforms, Q1 2021, observing improvements since 2018 but noting the market still needs to mature to be considered enterprise-ready. Key findings highlight that customers primarily use these solutions for supply chain security and self-monitoring, and there's a need for better transparency, dispute resolution, and integration with existing security business processes. The report emphasizes that while useful, these ratings are not a substitute for comprehensive risk assessment and require external validation and better integration to realize their full potential.

title: Gartner predicts data storytelling will dominate BI by 2025
summary: Gartner predicts that data storytelling will become the dominant method for consuming analytics by 2025, largely replacing self-service BI. This shift is driven by the need to make analytics accessible to a broader audience, with 75% of data stories expected to be automatically generated using AI and machine learning. Automated data storytelling aims to overcome the limitations of traditional self-service analytics and the scarcity of data experts, making data insights more consumable for business users.

title: 4 lessons on designing responsible, ethical tech: Microsoft case study
summary: This article details four key lessons from Microsoft's experience in designing responsible and ethical technology, highlighting how the company operationalized ethics in AI. It emphasizes the importance of culture change, effective tools, accountability through employee alignment, and the development of better, more inclusive products. The case study, jointly authored by the World Economic Forum and the Markkula Center for Applied Ethics, offers insights for other organizations aiming to close the "intention-action gap" in technological innovation.

title: Why Are Google and Facebook Now Okay with Australia’s News Media Bargaining Code?
summary: Google and Facebook have come to terms with Australia's News Media Bargaining Code, which mandates payment to news publishers. While initially opposed, their agreements with major news organizations and the inclusion of a compulsory mediation stage have made the legislation more palatable. The Code aims to address the significant bargaining power imbalance between digital platforms and news media, potentially leading to substantial financial contributions for journalism, though concerns remain about media diversity and the focus on larger publishers.

title: Nvidia CEO confident in company's growth prospects even if Arm acquisition does not happen
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang expressed confidence in the company's long-term growth trajectory, even if its acquisition of chip designer Arm is blocked by regulators. Huang emphasized that Nvidia's growth in areas like AI, autonomous vehicles, and 5G edge computing is independent of the Arm deal. Despite this, he remains confident that the $40 billion acquisition of Arm will be completed, believing it will significantly accelerate Arm's roadmap and benefit the ecosystem.

title: HP to acquire gaming peripherals company HyperX for $425 million
summary: HP announced its acquisition of HyperX, a gaming peripherals company previously owned by Kingston, for $425 million. This move is expected to strengthen HP's position in the growing PC hardware and gaming peripherals market, complementing its successful OMEN and Pavilion Gaming lines. The deal is set to close in Q2 2021, with Kingston retaining its DRAM, flash, and SSD businesses.

title: Major investment in Serbian Azure Data team
summary: Microsoft Development Center Serbia (MDCS) is expanding its Azure Data team with 60 new positions, a 30% increase for the team and 20% for MDCS overall, thanks to a significant investment. This expansion aims to strengthen existing products and launch new initiatives, enhancing Microsoft's position in the global market. Dragan Tomić, Director of MDCS, highlights the benefits for both the local IT community and Serbia as a whole, emphasizing job creation, high salaries, and the development of valuable expertise.

title: Vuzix says M400 and M4000 Smart Glasses now Microsoft Teams compatible
summary: Vuzix Corporation announced that its M400 and M4000 Smart Glasses are now compatible with Microsoft Teams, a widely used video conferencing application with 115 million average daily users. This integration allows Vuzix to target a significant segment of enterprise customers who rely on Microsoft Teams for hands-free communication. Vuzix will host a sales webinar and live demonstration to showcase the Microsoft Teams user experience on their smart glasses.

title: Microsoft Appoints Dr. HOU Yang as the Chairman & CEO, Greater China Region
summary: Microsoft Corporation has announced the appointment of Dr. HOU Yang as the new Chairman and CEO for the Greater China Region, effective July 1, to succeed Alain Crozier. Dr. Hou, previously a Senior Vice President at Qualcomm, brings extensive experience in the technology industry, partner development, and local market insight. Alain Crozier, who led Microsoft GCR since 2016 and significantly grew its cloud services and investments in the region, will transition to a new role to be announced soon.

title: Next-generation factory opens on UWM’s campus
summary: The Connected Systems Institute (CSI) at the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee has launched its first industry testbed and production line, located in the Golda Meir Library building. This facility, along with a Digital Twin Laboratory, allows students and researchers to simulate and execute solutions for manufacturing challenges using connected systems and the industrial internet of things (IIoT). Supported by partners like Rockwell Automation and Microsoft, the CSI aims to boost U.S. industry by integrating advanced technology and training the future workforce.

title: Microsoft Appoints Dr. HOU Yang as the Chairman & CEO, Greater China Region
summary: Microsoft Corporation announced the appointment of Dr. HOU Yang as the new Chairman and CEO for its Greater China Region, succeeding Alain Crozier. Dr. Hou Yang previously served as Senior Vice President of the Semiconductor business at Qualcomm, where he significantly grew revenue in China. He will assume sole responsibility on July 1, after an onboarding period with Crozier.

title: Wearable Device Maker Huami Steps Out of Xiaomi’s Shadow
summary: Huami Corp. is rebranding outside China to Zepp Health Corp. and changing its ticker symbol to ZEPP, indicating a strategic move away from its long-standing relationship with Xiaomi. This rebranding is supported by a series of global acquisitions, investments, and partnerships aimed at establishing its own identity and improving its financial margins, which have been pressured by its association with Xiaomi. Despite declaring independence, Huami recently extended its "most preferred partner" status agreement with Xiaomi, highlighting a cautious approach to separation.

title: ST launches next gen power-saving microcontrollers
summary: STMicroelectronics has introduced its new STM32U5 series of power-saving microcontrollers (MCUs), designed for demanding smart applications like wearables and home automation, utilizing 40nm process geometry. These MCUs incorporate an Arm Cortex-M33 core and advanced security features, including hardware-based protection and graphic accelerators. They achieve low dynamic power consumption of less than 19µA/MHz and offer advanced security features, such as hardware-resistant encryption and secure data storage, addressing the growing need for power efficiency and strong security in IoT devices.

title: Vuzix announces support for Microsoft Teams on its M400 and M4000 Smart Glasses
summary: Vuzix Corporation has announced that its M400 and M4000 Smart Glasses now support Microsoft Teams, enabling hands-free video conferencing for enterprise customers. This integration aims to tap into Microsoft Teams' large user base, further expanding Vuzix's reach in the enterprise market. The company plans to host a webinar and live demonstration to showcase the Microsoft Teams user experience on its smart glasses.

title: Microsoft Teams SIP Phone Gateway preview and supported SIP phones announced
summary: Microsoft announced the preview of the Microsoft Teams SIP Phone Gateway, expanding support for native registration of specific SIP phones to Microsoft Teams. This gateway will allow certain models from Cisco, Poly, Yealink, and AudioCodes to integrate with Teams, offering functionalities like inbound/outbound calls, call transfer, and voicemail indicators. The initiative aims to leverage existing SIP phone infrastructure, particularly for former Skype for Business users, as Microsoft continues to develop more affordable Teams-native phones.

title: Companies That Prioritize Workforce Investment and Training Outperform Those That Don’t
summary: This article highlights that companies investing in workforce development and training outperform those that do not, based on an analysis of Russell 1000 companies. The top quintile of companies in terms of Workforce Investment and Training scores outperformed the bottom quintile by 5.01% over the past year. This underscores the importance of employee advancement, skills development, and educational opportunities for improved business outcomes like productivity and customer satisfaction.

title: Threat Assessment: Active Exploitation of Four Zero-Day Vulnerabilities in Microsoft Exchange Server
summary: This article details the active exploitation of four zero-day vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-26855, CVE-2021-26857, CVE-2021-26858, and CVE-2021-27065) in Microsoft Exchange Server by multiple threat actors. The vulnerabilities allow attackers to gain remote access, execute commands, and establish persistence via webshells, leading to credential theft and data exfiltration. Palo Alto Networks advises immediate patching and outlines various product-specific courses of action for protection against these threats.

title: Anghami goes public on NASDAQ via SPAC
summary: Music streaming platform Anghami is going public on NASDAQ through a merger with special purpose acquisition company (SPAC) Vistas Media Acquisition Company (VMAC), making it the first Arab technology startup to do so. The transaction values Anghami at $220 million and is expected to close in Q2 2021, providing the company with $142 million in cash for growth. Anghami, founded in 2012, has seen significant revenue growth and aims to expand its user base and technology development after the listing.

title: Changing Of The Guard For HPC And Big Iron At HPE
summary: Pete Ungaro, the long-time head of Cray and then HPE's High Performance Computing & Mission Critical Solutions group, is stepping down, with Justin Hotard taking over. This leadership change occurs as HPE continues to navigate a challenging market, focusing on profitability and leveraging the Cray acquisition to scale its HPC business. The company is making strategic bets on services and utility-style pricing for on-premises systems, with recent financial results indicating these efforts are beginning to pay off despite overall revenue and profit declines in some segments.

title: Qualys confirms data breach related to Accellion after documents leak
summary: Cloud security firm Qualys has confirmed a data breach stemming from a zero-day exploit in the Accellion FTA file transfer platform, which Qualys used for customer support. The breach did not impact Qualys' production environments or customer data hosted on its cloud platform, but documents related to customers were posted by the Clop ransomware gang on the Dark Web. Qualys had deployed the Accellion FTP server in a segregated DMZ environment and engaged FireEye Mandiant to investigate the incident.

title: Schlumberger New Energy, Chevron, and Microsoft Collaborate on Carbon Negative Bioenergy
summary: Schlumberger New Energy, Chevron, and Microsoft are partnering with Clean Energy Systems to develop a bioenergy with carbon capture and sequestration (BECCS) project in Mendota, California. This project aims to produce carbon-negative power by converting agricultural waste biomass into electricity and permanently storing over 99% of the CO2 emissions. The initiative is expected to remove approximately 300,000 tons of CO2 annually, contributing to improved air quality and creating jobs in the Central Valley.

title: Chevron deepens carbon-capture push with Microsoft, Schlumberger linkage
summary: Chevron Corp. is partnering with Microsoft Corp., Schlumberger New Energy, and Clean Energy Systems to build a carbon capture plant in Mendota, California. This initiative is part of Chevron's strategy to invest in renewables and other technologies, anticipating a shift in the energy market. The facility will convert agricultural biomass to electricity, with a process designed to achieve net-negative carbon emissions by consuming CO2 and permanently storing produced CO2 underground.

title: BUZZ, the ETF of Social-Media Darlings, Drops in Trading Debut
summary: The VanEck Vectors Social Sentiment ETF (BUZZ) began trading, aiming to capitalize on the retail-investing trend and the influence of social media buzz on stock performance. This ETF includes stocks like Tesla and DraftKings, aiming to capture the "new era of investing" where information is sourced and shared online.

title: Chevron to build California carbon capture plant with Microsoft, Schlumberger
summary: Chevron is partnering with Microsoft, Schlumberger, and Clean Energy Systems to construct a carbon capture plant in Mendota, California. This initiative aims to convert agricultural biomass into electricity while storing the resulting carbon underground, helping to reduce emissions and align with California's plan to phase out agricultural waste burning. Engineering and design work will commence immediately, with a final investment decision expected next year.

title: Microsoft and ZeniMax deal approved by US Securities and Exchange Commission
summary: The US Securities and Exchange Commission has approved Microsoft's acquisition of ZeniMax. This means the deal could close earlier than the anticipated June deadline, with the European Commission's decision now being the final hurdle. Microsoft initially announced the acquisition of ZeniMax, parent company to several notable game studios, in September and created a subsidiary named Vault to aid in EU approval.

title: Lighthouses Live: Reimagining Operations for Growth
summary: This article discusses the World Economic Forum's "Global Lighthouse Network" initiative, which recognizes manufacturing leaders for their advanced adoption of Fourth Industrial Revolution technologies. It highlights discussions from a live event where company leaders, including Satya Nadella (Microsoft) and Alex Gorsky (Johnson & Johnson), shared insights on how digital transformation, accelerated by COVID-19, drives growth, resilience, and sustainability across various industries. Key themes included the importance of digital capability for resilience, putting sustainability at the center of business strategy, and fostering a digital mindset throughout the workforce.

title: Microsoft, Wells Fargo satisfied Trump Labor Department on hiring more Black employees
summary: The Trump administration's Labor Department closed inquiries into Microsoft and Wells Fargo after the companies provided satisfactory responses regarding their plans to hire more Black employees. These inquiries, initiated in September, asked for proof that their diversity hiring plans complied with antidiscrimination laws. Both companies had previously pledged to increase Black representation in their leadership and workforce following the killing of George Floyd in May.

title: Preparing for Retaliation Against Russia, U.S. Confronts Hacking by China (Published 2021)
summary: The Biden administration faces an escalating cyberconflict with both Russia and China. While preparing to retaliate against Russia for a large-scale hacking of government agencies, a new major breach in Microsoft systems by a state-sponsored Chinese group has emerged, challenging the administration's cyber strategy. The response to these incidents will define how President Biden tackles imposing penalties on rivals exploiting cyber vulnerabilities.

title: Quantum computing startup IonQ announces $2bn SPAC merger
summary: Quantum computing startup IonQ has announced a $2 billion merger with dMY Technology Group, Inc. III, a Special Purpose Acquisition Company (SPAC), making it the first publicly traded quantum computing company. Its shares are expected to trade on the NYSE under "IONQ." This move follows recent trends of data center-related companies utilizing SPACs for quicker market entry.

title: IonQ to become publicly traded pure quantum computing company
summary: Quantum computing firm IonQ Inc. announced its plan to go public through a merger with dMY Technology Group Inc. III, a special-purpose acquisition company, valuing IonQ at approximately $2 billion. Upon closing, IonQ will trade under the symbol "IONQ" and aims to commercialize quantum computing by making its services available via cloud platforms like Amazon Bracket and Microsoft Azure. The company plans to use the $650 million raised to continue research, miniaturize its technology, and develop modular quantum computers.

title: Will 'WCBR' Swing Upwards after the Microsoft Hack?
summary: Following a significant cyberattack on Microsoft customers, the WisdomTree Cybersecurity Fund (WCBR) could see increased investor interest. This hack, potentially state-sponsored, highlights the growing demand for cybersecurity solutions from corporations and governments. The breach is expected to lead to elevated spending on security, providing a long-term demand tailwind for the cybersecurity sector and WCBR.

title: Analyzing Attacks Against Microsoft Exchange Server With China Chopper Webshells
summary: This article analyzes attacks against Microsoft Exchange Server using China Chopper webshells, following the discovery of zero-day vulnerabilities exploited by the HAFNIUM group. It details the role of the China Chopper webshell, a lightweight backdoor injected into ASPX pages, and examines artifacts such as modification dates and "keys" within OAB configurations to understand attacker methodology, timing, and targeting patterns. The analysis reveals multiple clusters of threat actors, automated scanning, and variations in webshell code, suggesting diverse attack campaigns.

title: Will Zoom spell doom for business air travel?
summary: The article discusses the potential long-term impact of video conferencing platforms like Zoom on business air travel post-pandemic. While some experts predict a significant, permanent reduction in business trips due to the rise of remote work, others argue that in-person interactions and the "power of a handshake" remain crucial for building trust and closing deals. Airlines, heavily reliant on lucrative business travel revenue, face the challenge of adapting to a potentially shrunken market.

title: IonQ To Become The First Publicly Traded Pure-Play Quantum Computing Company
summary: IonQ announced its definitive merger agreement with dMY Technology Group III (NYSE: DMYI.U), which will result in IonQ becoming the first publicly traded pure-play quantum computing company on the NYSE under the symbol “IONQ”. The transaction is expected to generate $650 million in gross proceeds, including a $350 million PIPE investment from major institutional and strategic investors, leading to a pro forma implied market capitalization of approximately $2 billion. IonQ aims to leverage this capital to advance its mission of solving critical societal problems through quantum computing, with plans to develop networked modular quantum computers by 2023.

title: Tesla loses a third of its value for the third time in a year
summary: Tesla Inc.'s stock experienced its third significant drop in a year, losing a third of its value from its January record high, primarily due to investor concerns about rising interest rates affecting high-valuation stocks. The selloff wiped off nearly $300 billion from its market capitalization, moving it behind Facebook. This decline is more pronounced than other major tech companies, and its shares have steadily fallen since announcing a bitcoin purchase, even as bitcoin’s price climbed.

title: HPE’s Formation of HPE CTG Validates Organization-wide Commitment to Open 5G Mission
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) has formed the HPE Communications Technology Group (CTG) by combining its Telco Infrastructure team and Communications & Media Solutions (CMS) software portfolio. This move validates HPE's commitment to the Open 5G ecosystem, offering cloud-native platforms and extensive professional services to support CSPs in their 5G network builds. The CTG aims to differentiate HPE's solutions against both 5G infrastructure suppliers and public cloud providers by providing comprehensive integration and avoiding vendor lock-in.

title: Microsoft to explain what ZeniMax deal means for Game Pass subscribers on March 11
summary: Microsoft is set to explain the implications of its ZeniMax acquisition for Game Pass subscribers in a video presentation on March 11. While new game announcements are not expected, details on how the deal affects gamers and Game Pass members will be shared, including the addition of some Bethesda titles to the service and future internal studio games launching on Game Pass. The presentation will not cover exclusivity or presence on other platforms like PlayStation, and Microsoft has not yet publicly confirmed the closing of the $7.5 million deal.

title: The 10 most innovative corporate social responsibility companies of 2021
summary: This article highlights the top 10 most innovative companies in corporate social responsibility for 2021, recognizing their bold efforts to improve communities and the environment. It details initiatives from companies like Microsoft, which aims for carbon neutrality by 2030 and to remove all historical emissions by 2050, and Grove Collaborative, committed to eliminating plastic from its products. These companies are setting new benchmarks in sustainability and social impact.

title: Remediation Steps for the Microsoft Exchange Server Vulnerabilities
summary: This article details remediation steps for four critical zero-day Microsoft Exchange Server vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-26855, CVE-2021-26857, CVE-2021-26858, and CVE-2021-27065) discovered in March 2021. It provides a playbook for enterprises, emphasizing locating and patching all affected Exchange Servers, securing them with temporary mitigations if immediate patching is not possible, and determining if a server has already been compromised due to prior active exploitation. The guidance also includes engaging an incident response team if a compromise is suspected.

title: Inside Volatility Trading: Market Cycles
summary: This article discusses market cycles, particularly focusing on the period since March 2009. It examines the relationship between interest rates and equity markets, the behavior of volatility markets (VIX Index), and the impact of central bank policies. The author also delves into investment realities, the imperfection of financial models, and the current state of equity, bond, commodities, and housing markets.

title: Video Games & Esports: Building on 2020’s Rapid Growth
summary: The video game industry experienced significant growth in 2020, driven by the pandemic, new console releases, and the rise of social gaming, with total revenue reaching $175 billion. This article explores key trends poised to continue this expansion, including the increasing impact of digital distribution, the monetization strategies of free-to-play games, the evolution of social gaming into metaverse-like experiences, and the growing prominence of mobile gaming. It also highlights the role of game engines in facilitating development for smaller studios and concludes that the industry is set for continued strong performance and investor opportunities.

title: AMD and Xilinx Set to Merge Before the End of 2021, Looks Promising
summary: Rival chipmakers Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) and Xilinx are proceeding with a $35 billion all-stock merger, expected to finalize by the end of 2021. The deal will see AMD shareholders owning 74% of the new entity and Xilinx shareholders 26%, with Xilinx stockholders receiving 1.734 shares of AMD for each of their shares. This merger aims to diversify AMD's product portfolio and strengthen its position in computer processors, particularly in data centers and wireless networks.

title: Patent Filings Roundup: Fintiv Dooms CBMs; Canadian Process Ends IPR; New and Old NPE Campaigns Filed
summary: This article summarizes recent patent filings, noting a decrease in PTAB filings compared to district court patent litigation. It highlights key rulings, including the termination of CBM proceedings against Boom! Payments due to a Federal Circuit 101 ruling and the PTAB's denial of a petition based on Canadian service-of-process precedent. The piece also details new and continuing patent enforcement campaigns by various entities, including a significant increase in DynaIP subsidiary litigation.

title: Datto buys Israeli cybersecurity co BitDam
summary: US cybersecurity company Datto Inc. has acquired Israeli cybersecurity company BitDam. BitDam, founded in 2015 by Liron Barak and Maor Hizkiev, developed tools to protect against email-based attacks and had raised $3.5 million. This acquisition marks Datto's first in Israel and aims to enhance its security offerings for managed service providers (MSPs).

title: Dover Releases Content Management Platform
summary: Dover Fueling Solutions (DFS) has launched DX Promote, a new content management platform that transforms fuel dispensers into automated selling machines. This platform allows retailers to display locally targeted advertising for goods and services at each fueling point, aiming to drive customers into convenience stores. The system, driven by Microsoft Azure, enables central management and deployment of day and time-appropriate advertisements and initially launched with the DFS Anthem UX platform, now supporting Wayne Ovation and Wayne Helix fuel dispensers.

title: Hitesh Sheth
summary: This article features Hitesh Sheth, President and CEO of Vectra, detailing his extensive background in cybersecurity leadership roles at companies like Aruba Networks, Juniper Networks, Cisco, Liberate Technologies, Oracle, and Santa Cruz Operation. It also includes an article titled "Evolving Cybersecurity Takes More Than Money," which discusses the reactive nature of current cybersecurity responses to breaches like the Microsoft Exchange and SolarWinds incidents, advocating for a shift towards proactive, preventive measures in cybersecurity.

title: Procore Appoints Sandy Hoffman as VP of Diversity, Inclusion, and Belonging
summary: Procore Technologies Inc. has announced the appointment of Sandy Hoffman as its new VP of Diversity, Inclusion, and Belonging (DIBs). In this role, Hoffman will be responsible for developing and implementing initiatives to evolve Procore's culture of belonging and drive a more inclusive construction industry. She brings extensive experience from previous DIBs leadership positions at ServiceNow, LinkedIn, and Cisco.

title: UNFI branches out into bitcoin and a local marketplace
summary: United Natural Foods, Inc. (UNFI) is expanding its services by launching a local products marketplace for retailers and partnering with Coin Cloud to place bitcoin kiosks in grocery stores. The company reported strong Q2 earnings with adjusted earnings up 57% and net sales up 7.1%, driven by increased at-home consumption and successful cross-selling efforts. UNFI also extended its supply contract with Whole Foods until 2027 and expects to see significant inflation and promotional activity increase in the coming fiscal year.

title: Now it is F5’s turn to reveal critical security bugs – and the Feds were quick to sound the alarm on these BIG-IP flaws
summary: F5 has disclosed 21 vulnerabilities in its Big-IP products, with seven rated as critical, enabling potential remote code execution, denial of service, or complete system compromise. CISA issued an advisory urging immediate patching, while the FBI linked observed attacks exploiting Microsoft Exchange flaws to Chinese cyber actors targeting various U.S. sectors. The article details specific CVEs and their severity, emphasizing the need for prompt updates to affected F5 and BIG-IQ products.

title: Microsoft Exchange Server Attack Timeline: Discoveries and Mitigations
summary: This article details the timeline of the Microsoft Exchange Server zero-day vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-26855, CVE-2021-26857, CVE-2021-26858, CVE-2021-27065) and their exploitation. It highlights the discovery by DevCore in late 2020, early exploitation in January 2021 reported by Volexity and Dubex, and Microsoft's subsequent patch release on March 2, 2021. The article emphasizes that patching alone is insufficient due to prior exploitation and that multiple threat groups are actively leveraging these vulnerabilities.

title: ServiceNow enhances its Now Platform
summary: ServiceNow has launched its Now Platform Quebec release, introducing enhanced native AI capabilities and new low-code app development tools. This update aims to enable faster innovation, improved productivity, and enhanced experiences for customers by empowering users to build applications with varying technical skill levels. The platform further introduces Creator Workflows and new solutions for process optimization, workforce optimization, and enhanced employee experiences, helping organizations adapt to new ways of working and digital transformation challenges.

title: Threat Assessment: DearCry Ransomware
summary: DearCry is a new ransomware variant that exploits Microsoft Exchange Server's ProxyLogon vulnerabilities for initial access. It encrypts files using AES-256 and RSA-2048, modifies file headers to include 'DEARCRY!', and demands ransom via email contact rather than a fixed amount. Palo Alto Networks advises immediate updates for Microsoft Exchange Servers and outlines protective measures through their security products.

title: Microsoft Partner iLink Digital Acquires Salesforce Partner Dazeworks
summary: Global consulting company iLink Digital, a Microsoft Partner, has acquired a majority stake in Salesforce partner Dazeworks, according to an announcement on March 12, 2021. This acquisition is part of iLink's 2021 growth strategy to enhance its Salesforce expertise and service offerings. Dazeworks brings significant Salesforce implementation experience, including working with Fortune 50 companies and having the most Salesforce MVPs globally.

title: Technology and the Free Press: The Need for Healthy Journalism in a Healthy Democracy
summary: This article by Brad Smith, Vice Chair & President of Microsoft, discusses the critical relationship between technology and a healthy free press in a democracy. It highlights how technology, particularly the dominance of companies like Google in digital advertising and content aggregation, has negatively impacted the financial viability of journalism, especially local news. Smith advocates for a multi-faceted solution involving continued evolution within journalism, greater responsibility from tech companies, and government intervention through legislation modeled after Australia's recent law to restore competition and support news organizations.

title: Parametric Design Software Market Outlook 2021: Big Things are Happenings | PTC, SolidWorks, Autodesk, Siemens
summary: A report by AMA Research highlights a deep analysis of the global Parametric Design Software Market, including market characteristics, sizing, estimates, and growth segmentation. It discusses major players like PTC, SolidWorks, Autodesk, and Siemens, emphasizing the market's growth drivers such as rapid developments in design and manufacturing, and the increasing adoption of virtual platforms for product development, while also noting the restraint of high implementation costs. The study also covers market trends, regional breakdowns, and strategic developments for key competitors.

title: Energy efficient and scalable: NXP’s new EdgeVerse chips are aimed at industrial edge uses
summary: NXP Semiconductors expanded its EdgeVerse portfolio with new i.MX 8ULP, i.MX 8ULP-CS (cloud secured) with Microsoft Azure Sphere, and i.MX 9 series processors. These new chips feature the EdgeLock secure enclave for enhanced security and Energy Flex architecture for maximized energy efficiency, targeting industrial edge applications. The i.MX 9 series also integrates hardware neural processing units for accelerating machine learning at the edge.

title: Howard Marks says ETFs can't go on forever
summary: Howard Marks, co-founder of Oaktree Capital Management, believes that the trend of passive investing through ETFs cannot continue indefinitely. He argues that ETFs' automatic buying of large-cap tech stocks without fundamental analysis leads to overvaluation and advises individual investors to consider actively managed mutual funds. Marks also shared his evolving views on cryptocurrencies, acknowledging their growing demand despite lacking intrinsic value.

title: How Microsoft is invested in Israeli settler-colonialism
summary: This article examines Microsoft's deep involvement in Israeli militarism and settler-colonialism, highlighting how the company benefits from and contributes to violence through technology. It details Microsoft's historical presence in Israel, its investments in military-industrial complex startups, provision of essential computing services to Israeli forces, and critiques its public relations efforts to mask these activities. The piece argues that Microsoft's activities, masked by progressive branding and academic partnerships, bolster state violence while activists call for divestment.

title: AMD Unveils EPYC 'Milan' 7003 CPUs, Zen 3 Comes to 64-Core Server Chips
summary: AMD has officially launched its EPYC 'Milan' 7003 processors, bringing the Zen 3 architecture to the server market with its flagship 64-core EPYC 7763, claiming it to be the world's fastest server processor. These new 7nm chips are drop-in compatible with existing servers and offer significant performance improvements over Intel's Xeon Cascade Lake Refresh chips, particularly in HPC, Cloud, and enterprise workloads, alongside a better price-to-performance ratio. The Milan processors also focus on expanding AMD's hardware and software ecosystems to better cater to a broader range of enterprise customers.

title: AMD EPYC™ 7003 Series CPUs Set New Standard as Highest Performance Server Processor
summary: AMD has announced its new EPYC™ 7003 Series CPUs, including the EPYC 7763, which it claims is the world's highest-performing server processor. These processors leverage "Zen 3" cores to offer significant performance improvements across HPC, cloud, and enterprise workloads, alongside enhanced security features like Secure Encrypted Virtualization-Secure Nested Paging (SEV-SNP). The ecosystem for AMD EPYC processors is expected to expand considerably by the end of 2021 with new cloud instances and OEM platforms from major partners like AWS, Cisco, Dell, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure.

title: AMD Raises Bar Against Intel With 3rd-Gen EPYC Milan CPUS
summary: AMD has launched its third-generation EPYC processors, codenamed Milan, aiming to surpass Intel in performance and total cost of ownership for data centers. The new processors offer significant performance improvements, enhanced security features, and backward compatibility with existing server platforms, providing a competitive edge over Intel's upcoming Xeon Scalable chips. AMD emphasizes the value proposition of Milan through its high core density, strong price-performance ratio, and reduced TCO for cloud, enterprise, and HPC workloads.

title: The Future of Work is here – ready?
summary: The article discusses the accelerated shift to flexible and hybrid work models due to the pandemic, highlighting a study by Deloitte commissioned by Liberty Global. It explores themes such as the need for new "meta skillsets" in an automated world, the importance of agile leadership and clear communication, and the opportunity for greater diversity and inclusion through flexible work arrangements. The article also touches upon the evolving role of the office as a hub for collaboration and innovation, while acknowledging the need for a "skills revolution" to address potential societal divides in the new economic landscape.

title: If You Invested $1,000 In Microsoft 10 Years Ago, Here's How Much You'd Have Now
summary: This article examines the hypothetical growth of a $1,000 investment in Microsoft (MSFT) made ten years prior. It highlights Microsoft's business model, key products, and recent successes in cloud computing and acquisitions. The article concludes that such an investment would have yielded significant returns, emphasizing Microsoft's strong performance as a long-term investment.

title: Microsoft announces quarterly dividend
summary: Microsoft Corporation announced on March 16, 2021, that its board of directors declared a quarterly dividend of $0.56 per share. The dividend is scheduled to be paid on June 10, 2021, to shareholders of record as of May 20, 2021, with an ex-dividend date of May 19, 2021. The announcement highlights Microsoft's ongoing commitment to shareholder returns.

title: Nokia to cut up to 10,000 jobs worldwide
summary: Nokia plans to cut between 5,000 and 10,000 jobs globally over the next two years to reduce costs by €600m (£518m). The telecoms giant aims to invest in 5G, cloud computing, and digital infrastructure research to improve its performance against rivals. Job cuts are expected across various regions, with about 96 roles in the UK and 300 in Finland under threat.

title: AMD adds seven-nanometer Ryzen Pro 5000 processors for business laptops
summary: AMD has introduced its new Ryzen Pro 5000 series processors for business laptops, following the launch of new server chips. These seven-nanometer Zen 3 core processors include the top-end 5850U, which offers significant performance improvements and extended battery life compared to Intel's offerings. The Ryzen Pro 5000 series also incorporates advanced security and management features, such as shadow stack technology and Memory Guard, to protect corporate data and facilitate remote IT management.

title: 3 Stocks That Pass the Warren Buffett "Tides" Test
summary: This article identifies three companies, Microsoft, Costco, and American Express, that pass Warren Buffett's "tides test," meaning they are robust enough to perform well even during economic downturns. It discusses each company's business model, financial health, and reasons why they are considered strong, resilient investments, highlighting their ability to thrive amidst market volatility. The author suggests these stocks are suitable for those seeking safe-haven investments, especially during uncertain economic times.

title: EA’s mobile push continues with $2.4bn Glu acquisition
summary: Electronic Arts (EA) has agreed to acquire Glu Mobile Inc. for $2.4 billion, a move expected to significantly expand EA's mobile gaming portfolio and player base. The acquisition of Glu, known for its casual and free-to-play mobile games, will nearly double the size of EA's mobile business and is projected to increase its underlying profitability within the first year. This deal is part of a broader trend of consolidation in the video game industry, fueled by strong growth in mobile gaming, especially during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: AMD Strikes Back At Intel vPro With Ryzen Pro 5000 CPUs
summary: AMD has launched its new Ryzen Pro 5000 processors for business laptops, directly targeting Intel's vPro lineup. AMD claims these new CPUs offer superior multi-threaded performance, energy efficiency, and enterprise-grade security features that can compete "toe-to-toe" with Intel's offerings. The company expects a significant increase in commercial notebook design wins with these new chips.

title: Kick-Start Your Composable Business Journey With Two Key Strategies
summary: A majority of businesses are increasing their technology spending and prioritizing digital initiatives, driven by the pandemic. This research outlines two key strategies for application leaders to introduce composability into their software engineering environment immediately using existing resources, and to prepare for future strategic composition modeling. The goal is to boost application agility and business resilience.

title: Fidelity Magellan ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (BATS:FMAG)
summary: The Fidelity Magellan ETF (FMAG) is an actively managed, non-transparent ETF that invests in fundamentally selected firms globally, tracking the S&P 500 TR USD index. Launched in February 2021, the fund has assets under management of $266.85 million and a net expense ratio of 0.59%. Its top holdings include major tech companies like NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Amazon.com.

title: T-Mobile, AT&T, and Verizon to duel for 5G enterprise, business subscribers
summary: T-Mobile, AT&T, and Verizon are preparing for a battle over 5G business, enterprise, and edge computing subscribers, each with distinct strategies. T-Mobile aims to disrupt the market by applying its "Uncarrier" playbook to enterprise, targeting AT&T and Verizon's dominant business accounts. Verizon is focusing on integrating 5G with edge computing through partnerships with tech giants like AWS and Microsoft Azure, while AT&T is leveraging a hybrid network approach combining 5G with last-mile fiber to serve diverse customer segments.

title: At $2.08 Trillion, Apple Is Bigger Than These Things
summary: As of March 15, 2021, Apple Inc. (AAPL) boasts a market capitalization of $2.08 trillion, making it the world's largest public company. This staggering figure surpasses the GDP of most countries, the total market value of many global stock exchanges, the U.S. budget deficit, and the inflation-adjusted costs of multiple major U.S. wars. It also exceeds the combined net worth of the world's 18 richest people.

title: Ford to allow some employees work-from-home flexibility
summary: Ford Motor announced that it will offer a hybrid home-and-office work model to approximately 86,000 non-manufacturing global employees, effective from July for its U.S. workforce. This decision positions Ford as the latest major company to adopt flexible work arrangements in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic, following similar moves by tech giants like Microsoft, Salesforce.com, and Twitter. The change impacts a significant portion of its global staff, excluding those in manufacturing, research, product development, and design who continue to work on-site.

title: Imperva Snags Akamai’s Micheal McCollough To Lead Channels
summary: Imperva has hired Micheal McCollough, formerly Akamai's global channel chief, to lead and expand its channel business, with a focus on becoming a channel-first company. McCollough aims to strengthen relationships with public cloud providers, enhance services for existing partners, and leverage the company's acquisition of jSonar. He plans to incentivize partners through new programs, potentially driving almost all new business through the channel and increasing their involvement in services and support.

title: Space junk from satellites puts global networks at risk
summary: The increasing number of satellites in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) is creating a significant risk of collisions and space debris, threatening global communication networks. The article highlights past incidents, the challenges of tracking satellites, and the "Kessler Syndrome," where collisions could create cascading debris fields. While some private companies are developing mitigation strategies, there is currently no binding international framework to address this growing problem.

title: QYLG Stock Price | Global X Nasdaq 100 Covered Call & Growth ETF
summary: This article provides comprehensive information about the Global X Nasdaq 100 Covered Call & Growth ETF (QYLG), including its current stock price, trading exchange (NASDAQ), and key financial metrics like dividend yield, expense ratio, and market capitalization. It also features technical analysis indicators and a list of its top holdings, offering a detailed overview for potential investors.

title: Twitter share price history in recent times
summary: This article provides a historical overview of Twitter's share price performance since its 2013 IPO, detailing key events that impacted its stock movements. It covers the company's origins, monetization strategies, and significant ups and downs, including earnings reports, user growth challenges, acquisition rumors, and strategic announcements. The piece highlights how various factors, from initial market reception to technical glitches and ambitious growth plans, influenced investor sentiment and Twitter's valuation over time.

title: How DataStax Generated $1M in Pipeline using Priority Engine
summary: DataStax utilized Priority Engine to boost qualified demand and enable its sales team. Within the first five months, the company generated nearly $1 million in marketing-generated pipeline and 12 opportunities, alongside over $8 million in influenced pipeline and 58 influenced opportunities. This was achieved by identifying active, in-market prospects and leveraging prospect-level intent insights for hyper-targeted outreach and sales enablement.

title: How Citigroup is using leave policies to support employees amid the pandemic
summary: Citigroup has introduced new paid-leave programs, including a 12-week sabbatical at 25% pay and the option to purchase additional vacation days, to support employee well-being and work-life balance. These initiatives aim to address shifting employee expectations and combat burnout, recognizing the need for mental health support and community engagement opportunities. The company believes these policies will enhance employee engagement, retention, and attraction of top talent.

title: Cloud as an opportunity to fundamentally change the way we operate
summary: UBS has significantly advanced its cloud computing strategy, exceeding initial targets set in 2018. Over 50% of its computing is now in a hybrid cloud environment, enabled by a strategic partnership with Microsoft Azure in Switzerland. This transformation has enhanced agility, stability, and security, allowing UBS to better serve clients, manage peak loads, and adapt to unprecedented events like the pandemic.

title: Google Cloud Pricing vs AWS: A Fair Comparison?
summary: This article provides a detailed comparison of Google Cloud Platform (GCP) and Amazon Web Services (AWS) pricing for compute instances and storage. It highlights differences in market positioning, on-demand and reserved VM pricing, and various storage options, noting where direct comparisons can be misleading due to differing structures. The article also discusses cost optimization strategies using NetApp Cloud Volumes ONTAP.

title: Scammers trick Android users into installing fake, malware-laden Clubhouse app
summary: Scammers are exploiting the demand for the audio-based social app Clubhouse among Android users by distributing a fake, malware-laden version of the app. This fraudulent Android app, discovered by ESET researchers, contains a Trojan virus called "BlackRock" that can steal login information from over 458 online services, including financial apps, social media, and cryptocurrency exchanges, and can also intercept text messages, bypassing two-factor authentication. Experts warn that the absence of an official Android version of Clubhouse creates a significant vulnerability that cybercriminals are eager to exploit, making an official Android app the ultimate solution.

title: Microsoft to Ease Workers Back to the Office Starting Next Week (Published 2021)
summary: Microsoft announced its plan to begin reopening its Redmond, Wash., headquarters to some 57,000 nonessential employees starting the following week. This marks a significant step in the company's six-step "dial" system for returning to the office, allowing a hybrid work model. Microsoft anticipates that a hybrid work policy, with employees working from home less than 50% of the time, will become standard even after the pandemic no longer poses a significant burden.

title: Microsoft to start bringing workers back to Redmond headquarters
summary: Microsoft is planning to begin bringing employees back to its Redmond, Washington headquarters starting March 29. The tech giant will allow workers the choice to return to the office, continue remote work, or adopt a hybrid model, as Washington state moves into Phase 3 of its COVID-19 reopening plan. This decision follows Microsoft's monitoring of local health data.

title: FlexPod thinks inside and outside the box
summary: This article discusses how FlexPod technology continues to evolve by "thinking inside and outside the box," offering both traditional data center applications and innovative solutions. It highlights the benefits FlexPod provides to IT teams, such as improved application performance and reduced downtime, and details recent software enhancements like ONTAP integration with Cisco Intersight. The post also covers new reference architectures for VMware vSphere 7.0, Oracle 19c RAC, EHR, and Cisco VxLAN EVPN.

title: Is Salesforce Stock a Buy?
summary: Salesforce, a leading software-as-a-service company, has shown strong historical investment returns and continues to be considered a good buy due to its large market opportunity, robust financial performance, and innovative culture. The article highlights Salesforce's dominant position in the CRM market, its quick revenue growth, and its strategic acquisitions like Slack, despite potential integration challenges.

title: Hackers are exploiting new F5 bug in the wild
summary: Hackers have begun exploiting critical vulnerabilities in F5 Networks' BIG-IP software just days after the company disclosed them. Security researchers observed multiple exploitation attempts against honeypots, with proof-of-concept exploits appearing online. Organizations using F5 software are urged to patch their systems immediately, as the vulnerabilities could allow remote code execution and data deletion.

title: The Next Great Disruption Is Hybrid Work—Are We Ready?
summary: This article discusses the shift to hybrid work as the next major disruption following the sudden move to remote work. It highlights key trends from the 2021 Work Trend Index, emphasizing the permanency of flexible work, the disconnect between leaders and employees, rising digital exhaustion, challenges faced by Gen Z, shrinking professional networks impacting innovation, the rise of authenticity at work, and the broadening talent marketplace. The article concludes with strategies for leaders to navigate this transition effectively.

title: Quantum Brilliance unveils diamond-based quantum accelerator that can run at room temperature
summary: Quantum Brilliance has emerged from stealth mode to introduce the world's first diamond-based quantum accelerator that operates at room temperature. This innovation eliminates the need for extreme cooling or complex laser systems, which are typically required by existing quantum computers. The company aims to make quantum computing an "everyday technology" by developing hardware that can be installed in various environments, including data centers and even laptops, and will soon install its first accelerator at Australia's Pawsey Supercomputing Center.

title: Intel to invest $20B in Arizona expansion, add 3,000 jobs
summary: Intel announced a $20 billion investment to expand its campus in Chandler, Arizona, which is already considered the most advanced semiconductor factory globally. This expansion is expected to generate over 3,000 permanent high-tech jobs and an additional 3,000 construction jobs. The move signifies a major commitment by Intel to bolster its manufacturing capabilities in the U.S.

title: Get to Know AutoCAD 2022 – The Connected Design Experience
summary: AutoCAD 2022 introduces new features like Trace, Share, and Count to enhance collaboration, automation, and accuracy in design workflows. It also offers improved connectivity across devices (desktop, web, mobile) and with other Autodesk products and cloud storage providers. These updates aim to provide users with a more streamlined and efficient design experience.

title: Industrial giant Honeywell says it has ‘returned to service’ after cyber intrusion
summary: Honeywell, a Fortune 100 industrial giant, reported that a malware disruption affecting a limited number of its computer systems has been remediated, with services returned to normal. The company enlisted Microsoft's help and stated that it does not expect a material impact on its operations, nor has evidence yet emerged of data exfiltration from primary customer information systems. This incident follows an increasing trend of ransomware attacks in the manufacturing sector.

title: Tech Moves: Startup Haven grows team to lead new fund; PSL promotions; F5 Networks adds execs
summary: This article details significant "Tech Moves" in the Pacific Northwest, including Startup Haven launching a new investment fund and expanding its team. Pioneer Square Labs (PSL) announced three leadership promotions, and F5 Networks hired new executives and promoted an existing one. Additionally, various other Seattle-area companies like Redfin, Fabric, Impinj, Strike Graph, Reverb, and Curi Bio made key hires, promotions, or board appointments.

title: Intel to spend $20 billion on U.S. chip plants as CEO challenges Asia dominance
summary: Intel announced plans to invest $20 billion in two new chip manufacturing plants in Arizona, aiming to expand its advanced chip production and open its factories to outside customers. This move by CEO Pat Gelsinger directly challenges the dominance of TSMC and Samsung in the advanced chip market and seeks to shift the technological balance of power back to the U.S. and Europe. The company expects $72 billion in revenue and adjusted earnings per share of $4.55 for 2021, and the new strategy is intended to restore Intel's reputation and create 3,000 permanent jobs.

title: Independent cloud provider DigitalOcean drops in Wall Street debut
summary: DigitalOcean, a small-scale cloud infrastructure provider, debuted on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol "DOCN" with shares opening lower than their IPO price. The company raised $775 million in its IPO and aims to challenge larger cloud providers like Amazon and Microsoft by focusing on ease of use and personalized support for small and medium-sized businesses. Despite a net loss in 2020, DigitalOcean plans to increase operating margins and expand its data center footprint.

title: Newfound Popularity of Thematic ETFs
summary: Thematic ETFs, which invest in baskets of stocks benefiting from emerging trends, technology, or evolving economic landscapes, have seen a significant surge in popularity since October 2020, with AUM growing by 132%. Despite this growth, the article highlights potential risks associated with these ETFs, including the reversal of investor enthusiasm impacting fund flow and performance, the concentrated holdings of individual stocks within the ETFs, and the potential for misleading diversification that may dilute thematic exposure and justify higher fees. Investors are advised against chasing "hot" ETFs without understanding their underlying holdings and potential risks.

title: Corporates are increasingly hungry for data. How they get it is changing fast.
summary: S&P Global is transforming how it provides data to clients, shifting from traditional desktop environments to direct data feeds, APIs, and cloud-based solutions like Snowflake. This change is driven by corporates' increasing hunger for data to inform business decisions and unlock value. The company's acquisition of Kensho and the launch of the S&P Global Marketplace Workbench are central to this strategy, enabling more direct interaction with and integration of diverse datasets.

title: Tesla can now be bought for bitcoin, Elon Musk says
summary: Elon Musk announced that Tesla customers can now purchase its electric vehicles using Bitcoin, with availability expanding outside the US later this year. This decision follows Tesla's significant $1.5 billion investment in Bitcoin and marks a major step towards mainstream acceptance for the cryptocurrency. Musk also stated that Bitcoin payments received by Tesla would not be converted to traditional currency, signifying a direct embrace of the digital asset.

title: Fastest-Growing Major Cloud Vendors: Google #1, Oracle #2, Microsoft and ServiceNow #3
summary: Google Cloud leads as the fastest-growing major cloud vendor, while Oracle shows significant hypergrowth, ranking second. Microsoft and ServiceNow are tied for third. The article analyzes the cloud revenue growth rates of the world's top cloud providers, noting the impressive performance of Google and Oracle, and scrutinizing slower growth figures from IBM and SAP.

title: AI is boring - or is it?
summary: This article argues that the term "Artificial Intelligence" is overused and often misapplied to simple technologies, creating inflated expectations. Despite the hype, the author, Christian Ott, emphasizes that the underlying AI technology is genuinely transformative, particularly in industries like automotive and manufacturing. He concludes that the real challenge and value of AI lie in effective data management from edge to core to cloud, allowing for scalable and impactful implementations.

title: Scott Belsky: What It Takes to Keep Your Business Ahead of the Pace of Technology
summary: Scott Belsky, Adobe's chief product officer and co-founder of Behance, shares insights on how businesses can stay ahead of technological advancements. He emphasizes building incubation labs, focusing hiring on creative problem-solvers rather than those skilled at mundane tasks, and leveraging technology to enhance customer experience. Belsky's advice centers on integrating new tech tools and continuously improving digital interactions to foster innovation and productivity.

title: Invesco unveils Nasdaq ‘next generation’ ETF
summary: Invesco has launched two new ETFs, the Invesco NASDAQ Next Generation 100 UCITS ETF (EQJS) and the Invesco Nasdaq-100 Swap UCITS ETF (EQQS), expanding its tech ETF range. EQJS tracks the Nasdaq Next Generation 100 index, mirroring a US-listed strategy, while EQQS provides synthetic exposure to the Nasdaq 100, designed to mitigate withholding tax on US equity dividends. These new offerings are listed on the LSE with competitive total expense ratios.

title: Message for students 2021:Ryoji Miyazaki
summary: Ryoji Miyazaki, a researcher at NEC's System Platform Research Laboratories, discusses his work on quantum annealing, a type of quantum computing. He highlights NEC's collaborative research efforts with external companies like D-Wave Systems Inc., Sigma-i Co., Ltd., and Parity Quantum Computing GmbH, aiming for practical application by 2023. Miyazaki also shares his positive experience working at NEC, emphasizing the diverse research environment, the company's historical contributions to quantum technology, and the freedom he finds in corporate research compared to academia.

title: Dover Launches DX Monitor for Remote Management
