summary: Dover Fueling Solutions (DFS) has launched DX Monitor, a new platform for remote monitoring and management of fuel dispensers and their components across customer sites. This system, part of the DFS DX connected solutions platform powered by Microsoft Azure, provides operators with dashboards, alerts, and reports to proactively manage maintenance and ensure continuous operations. The goal is to enhance productivity, efficiency, and customer experience at fueling stations.

title: How API-everything, developer creativity, and low code is the apex of IT agility
summary: This article discusses how an agile IT infrastructure, powered by APIs, developer creativity, and low-code solutions, is crucial for businesses to quickly adapt and innovate, especially during times of disruption. It highlights Adobe's approach with offerings like Adobe Experience Platform and Project Firefly, which enable developers to build custom applications efficiently. The piece also emphasizes the role of low-code development in empowering citizen developers and streamlining digital transformation.

title: The building blocks of Microsoft’s responsible AI program
summary: Microsoft emphasizes that for AI to benefit everyone, it must be developed and used in ways that earn trust. The company has established a robust governance model, including the Aether Committee and an Office of Responsible AI, to proactively set guardrails for AI systems. Microsoft also implements a "Responsible AI Standard" and a sensitive uses review process, which has led to drawing "red lines" for certain AI applications like real-time facial recognition for body cameras, underlining the importance of ethical considerations and industry-wide regulation.

title: Bain Capital infuses $750 million of funding into Nutanix
summary: Bain Capital has invested $750 million in Nutanix, recognizing its technology differentiation, growth potential, and transition to a subscription model. Executive David Humphrey noted Nutanix's leadership in the hyperconverged infrastructure market and its compelling vision for a hybrid cloud platform. This investment, in the form of convertible senior notes, aims to support Nutanix's continued growth, with Bain Capital representatives joining the board.

title: The China challenge: Why Intel is too strategic to fail
summary: This article analyzes Intel's strategic shift to IDM 2.0 under CEO Pat Gelsinger, focusing on the company's plan to leverage internal manufacturing, external foundries, and a new Intel Foundry Services division. It examines the market changes impacting Intel, the critical threat from China's semiconductor ambitions, and the need for significant partnerships, including with IBM and the U.S. government, for Intel to regain its leadership and combat the China challenge. The authors argue that despite positive steps, Intel needs even more substantial changes, possibly a joint venture with a volume leader like Samsung, to succeed.

title: Schlumberger and Microsoft Expand Partnership to Bring Open, Enterprise-Scale Data Management to the Energy Industry
summary: Schlumberger and Microsoft have expanded their strategic partnership to accelerate new technologies for the energy industry. They have launched the Schlumberger Enterprise Data Management Solution for the OSDU Data Platform, an industry standard for energy data, which is available globally on Microsoft Azure. This collaboration aims to enhance data access and AI capabilities, driving productivity increases and performance gains across the energy sector.

title: HP aims to deliver highly personalized customer service and build customer loyalty
summary: HP is leveraging Microsoft Dynamics 365 Marketing to enhance its customer service by providing agents with a 360-degree view of customer journeys and needs. This initiative aims to deliver highly personalized support, improve customer loyalty, and optimize operational efficiency by reducing support call times and lowering costs. Through customer-led journey orchestration, HP plans to streamline interactions and ensure customers feel valued and understood.

title: Broadcom manages soaring customer growth with Oracle Cloud
summary: Broadcom successfully transitioned to Oracle Sales, Oracle CPQ, and Oracle DataFox Data Management to handle increased customer volume and a new business model after several major acquisitions. This move enabled them to integrate systems, migrate customer data, automate renewals, and improve sales efficiency within a tight deadline, avoiding the extension of a legacy CRM license. The Oracle solutions provided a unified customer view, reduced IT complexity, and enhanced sales operations, including significant improvements in sales compensation accuracy and staff retention.

title: Latest Round of Funding Values ServiceTitan at $8.3 Billion
summary: ServiceTitan, a leading software provider for the trades, announced a $500 million funding round at an $8.3 billion valuation, led by Tiger Global Management and Sequoia Capital Global Equities. This investment, the largest for any private vertical software company, will fuel rapid growth, customer experience, product development, and hiring. The company has surpassed $250 million in annual recurring revenue and serves over 7,500 contracting businesses.

title: Infosys and LivePerson Announce First-of-its-Kind Partnership to Drive Customer Experience Transformation for the World's Biggest Brands
summary: Infosys and LivePerson have formed a strategic partnership to revolutionize customer experience by integrating Infosys Cobalt with LivePerson's Conversational Cloud and AI. This collaboration aims to help major brands enhance customer and employee interactions through AI-powered conversations across various messaging channels. The initiative is expected to drive higher sales, improve customer satisfaction, and reduce operational costs for enterprises.

title: Micron Bails, Intel Does Optane Alone
summary: Micron has exited its partnership with Intel on 3D XPoint memory, selling its fab and writing off billions, leaving Intel to continue with Optane technology alone. The 3D XPoint memory, designed to be faster than flash and cheaper than DRAM, faced challenges in market acceptance due to high costs and interface limitations, despite its promising technical specifications. Intel's new CEO Pat Gelsinger will now decide the future of Optane, while customers reliant on the technology face increased supply risk.

title: Durable Objects, now in Open Beta
summary: Cloudflare announced that Durable Objects are now in open beta, available to all Cloudflare Workers® subscribers. Durable Objects provide coordination across multiple Workers and strongly consistent edge storage, enabling developers to build stateful serverless applications with ease. The article also details the competitive pricing model for compute and storage, highlighting significant cost savings compared to other major cloud providers.

title: SmartETFs Dividend Builder ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:DIVS) $DIVS
summary: The SmartETFs Dividend Builder ETF (DIVS) is an actively-managed ETF focusing on dividend-paying companies from developed and emerging markets, seeking income and consistent dividend growth. Launched on March 30, 2012, and managed by SmartETFs, the fund currently has $38.29 million in assets under management. Its top holdings include Texas Instruments, Cisco Systems, and Broadcom.

title: MicroVision (MVIS) Stock Forecast: Will Microsoft Buy the Company?
summary: MicroVision (MVIS) stock surged over 50 percent on March 31, 2021, driven by rumors of potential acquisition interest from tech giants like Apple and Microsoft, especially after Microsoft secured a $22 billion contract with the U.S. Army for augmented reality headsets, in which MicroVision is believed to be a supplier. Despite this growth, MVIS remains a speculative investment due to its low revenue, lack of analyst coverage, and high volatility, with its CEO acknowledging the company is "up for sale."

title: Delta, Coca-Cola blast home state Georgia's voting restrictions as 'unacceptable'
summary: Coca-Cola Co and Delta Air Lines, along with Microsoft Corp and Citi, have publicly criticized Georgia's new voting restrictions, calling them "unacceptable" and saying they unfairly restrict voting rights. The Republican-backed law, which has been slammed by President Biden and faces legal challenges, strengthens identification requirements and shortens early voting periods. This move comes after activists called for boycotts against companies for not opposing the law earlier, with Delta's criticism marking a reversal from an earlier statement.

title: Intermedia IPO Delayed; Cloud Service Provider Cites "Adverse" IPO Market
summary: Intermedia Cloud Communications Inc. has postponed its initial public offering, citing "adverse conditions" in the current IPO market. CEO Michael Gold stated that while there was strong investor interest, the company believes current market conditions would limit the IPO's opportunity. Intermedia, backed by Madison Dearborn Partners, had planned to raise up to $366 million, valuing the company at $1.5 billion, and reported revenues of $251.6 million in 2020.

title: Insight Public Sector Named as Principal Technology Partner for Cyber Bytes
summary: Insight Public Sector has partnered with the Cyber Bytes Foundation to launch the Advanced Technology Labs at the Quantico Cyber Hub in Stafford, Virginia. This initiative will bring together technology experts, equipment, and training from 15 leading global solutions providers to serve various government agencies, nonprofits, businesses, colleges, and universities. The Quantico Cyber Hub aims to accelerate the adoption of advanced cyber technologies and enhance the cyber workforce.

title: Philip Morris International Picks Cloud-Based Transportation Management Solution
summary: Philip Morris International (PMI) has selected Blue Yonder's SaaS- and cloud-based transportation management solution (TMS) to enhance its end-to-end supply chain strategy. This move aims to provide better visibility and control of product stocks, supporting the global commercialization of its smoke-free products. The solution, powered by Microsoft Azure, will allow PMI to manage global freight more efficiently across various transportation modes, improving service to both B2B and B2C customers.

title: Bilibili’s $123 million investment in TapTap plans to revolutionize game distribution in China
summary: Chinese video-sharing website Bilibili has invested $123 million in TapTap, aiming to disrupt traditional game distribution channels in China. TapTap stands out by not charging a commission on in-app purchases, a direct challenge to the commission models of major app stores like Huawei, Xiaomi, Google, and Apple. This move allows Bilibili to diversify its revenue and directly compete with giants like Tencent, Huawei, and Xiaomi in the highly competitive Chinese gaming market.

title: Compass CEO Robert Reffkin who pivoted from Goldman to tech faces tough IPO
summary: Robert Reffkin, CEO of the tech-focused brokerage Compass, successfully completed a challenging IPO, raising $450 million despite tech market headwinds. The company, which attracted funding from SoftBank, aims for profitability after recording $270 million in losses last year, leveraging its strategy of empowering real estate agents with technology. Reffkin's significant stake makes him one of the wealthiest Black entrepreneurs to take a venture-backed company public.

title: US Army awards Microsoft $22 billion IVAS contract to deliver Augmented Reality technology to US Soldiers
summary: The US Army has awarded Microsoft a fixed-price production agreement for the Integrated Visual Augmentation System (IVAS), valued at up to $21.88 billion over 10 years. This contract transitions IVAS from rapid prototyping to production, aiming to deliver over 120,000 augmented reality devices based on Microsoft's HoloLens to the Army's Close Combat Force. These devices will enhance situational awareness, night vision, and enable life-like mixed reality training for soldiers.

title: Microsoft Awarded IVAS Production Contract
summary: The US Army has awarded Microsoft Corporation a production contract for the Integrated Visual Augmentation System (IVAS). This agreement will transition IVAS to production and rapid fielding, aiming to provide next-generation night vision and situational awareness capabilities to the Close Combat Force. This partnership highlights accelerated prototype development through a Soldier Centered Design approach and leverages augmented reality and machine learning for enhanced training environments.

title: New Fabs Crop Up Globally in 2021 as Chip Crisis Continues
summary: Amidst the ongoing global chip crisis affecting various industries, several major semiconductor manufacturers are announcing significant expansion plans. Intel is investing $20 billion in two new fabs in Arizona and launching Intel Foundry Services, while GlobalFoundries is committing $1.4 billion to boost its global production capacity. SK Hynix has also received approval to build a massive $106.35 billion fab complex in South Korea, primarily for DRAM production.

title: 2020 Phishing Trends With PDF Files
summary: This article details the dramatic 1,160% increase in malicious PDF files observed from 2019 to 2020, reaching over 5 million files. It identifies five primary phishing schemes used by attackers: Fake Captcha, Coupon, Play Button, File Sharing, and E-commerce. The report also highlights the common tactic of traffic redirection used in these PDF phishing campaigns to evade detection and maintain the longevity of their lures.

title: Airbus Ventures Commends Quantum Computing Leader, IonQ, Inc., on Upcoming Public Debut
summary: Airbus Ventures congratulates IonQ, Inc. on its upcoming merger with dMY Technology Group, Inc. III, which will make IonQ the world’s first publicly traded pure-play quantum computing hardware and software company. Airbus Ventures, a key investor, supports IonQ's scalable roadmap towards developing modular quantum computers and addressing complex challenges in various industrial sectors, including aerospace and green energy. IonQ aims for broad quantum advantage by 2025.

title: Taste the Transformation: How Coca Cola is Building a Digital-First Business
summary: Coca-Cola is undergoing a significant digital transformation to reverse declining revenues, focusing on experience, operational, business, and cultural changes. Key initiatives include AI-powered vending machines that personalize experiences and organizational shifts to increase agility and leverage data during the COVID-19 pandemic. The company aims to become a digital-first business by integrating technology into all aspects of its operations and customer engagement.

title: Caledonia Mining ups dividend again, says Central Shaft is fully operational
summary: Caledonia Mining Corporation PLC increased its quarterly dividend for the fifth time in 18 months, raising it to 12 US cents. This decision stems from the anticipated combination of rising production and declining capital investment as their six-year investment program at Blanket mine concludes. Furthermore, the company announced that its new Central Shaft at the mine, the deepest gold mine shaft in Zimbabwe, is now fully operational, which is expected to resolve hoisting constraints and facilitate the expansion of mine capacity to target 80,000 ounces of gold production per year.

title: Gelsinger Leads Emboldened Intel With Ice Lake Launch
summary: Intel's new CEO, Pat Gelsinger, has launched the 3rd Gen Xeon Scalable processors, "Ice Lake," aimed at reasserting the company's dominance in the server chip market. These new chips feature integrated AI acceleration and security capabilities, backed by strong support from OEMs and public cloud providers. Gelsinger also outlined his "IDM 2.0" strategy, including a $20 billion plan to expand manufacturing fabs and the re-establishment of a major annual event, Intel On, to showcase the company's capabilities.

title: Intel Sets Ice Lake Apart From AMD EPYC With AI, Systems Approach
summary: Intel has launched its third-generation Xeon Scalable CPUs, codenamed Ice Lake, emphasizing AI and cryptography acceleration and a comprehensive systems approach to compete with AMD's EPYC processors. Despite AMD's higher core counts, Intel highlights its processors' performance gains in specific AI, cloud, and HPC workloads due to specialized accelerators and software optimizations. Intel's strategy also includes a broader product portfolio and continuous software enhancements to improve overall data center performance and efficiency.

title: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon annual letter: How Wall Street will remote work, for better or worse
summary: Jamie Dimon, CEO of JPMorgan Chase, outlined his vision for a post-pandemic work culture in his annual shareholder letter, stating that he expects no more than 10% of JPMorgan employees to permanently work from home. While embracing remote work trends, he also expressed concerns about its potential negative effects on new employees, decision-making speed, and company creativity. Dimon anticipates a significant reduction in bank corporate real estate and a move to more open seating arrangements, while still planning to build a new headquarters in New York City.

title: Intel unveils highest performing data-center processors, made with Israel team
summary: Intel has launched its new Ice Lake Server processors, which are optimized for cloud and high-end computing and promise 46% higher performance than the previous generation. These processors, developed in Haifa and produced in Kiryat Gat, Israel, include built-in AI capabilities, encryption, and cybersecurity features. All major cloud service providers, including Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and Dell, plan to offer services powered by these new Intel processors in 2021.

title: Bot Wars | Entrepreneur reimagines how we work
summary: TC Energy is implementing Robotic Process Automation (RPA) through its "Citizen Development program," led by engineer Francisco Igor Paniagua Anguiano. This initiative aims to empower employees to automate low-value, repetitive tasks using tools like MS Power Automate Desktop, freeing them to focus on more complex work. A pilot program, "Bot Wars," successfully engaged 16 Canada Gas employees who developed seven bots, showcasing the program's potential to drive efficiency and foster innovation across the organization.

title: Trifacta unveils new integrations to enable data wrangling
summary: Trifacta has introduced new integrations and an updated tool to enhance data wrangling capabilities, particularly within Google BigQuery. These updates allow users to perform data preparation directly in BigQuery using SQL, integrate with dbt Core for building data pipelines, and partner with Databricks to streamline data preparation for analytics and machine learning. The goal is to provide more flexible, efficient, and user-driven data engineering solutions, appealing to both existing and potential Trifacta customers.

title: KKR invests $500 mln in cloud storage firm Box, gets board seat
summary: Private equity firm KKR & Co Inc will invest $500 million in cloud storage company Box Inc and receive a board seat. This investment, made through convertible preferred stock, concludes Box's strategic review and intends to address pressure from hedge fund Starboard Value LP regarding its stock performance, allowing Box to remain a public company and focus on expanding its cloud services. Box plans to use the funds for a share buyback, enabling Starboard to cash out its stake.

title: Arista simplifies network management in latest CloudVision
summary: Arista Networks has updated its CloudVision software to simplify cloud-based network management through a new graphical user interface and built-in workflows. The CloudVision 2021 upgrade also improves AI-powered analytics for identifying network congestion and offers enhanced application monitoring for popular services like Microsoft 365, Salesforce, and Zoom. These enhancements aim to reduce IT complexity, especially for managing remote workers, and compete with simpler offerings from Cisco and Juniper.

title: Moj, ShareChat-parent latest to join Unicorn club, raises $502 million in latest funding round
summary: Mohalla Tech, the parent company of Moj and ShareChat, has achieved unicorn status after raising $502 million in a funding round led by Lightspeed Ventures and Tiger Global. This investment values the company at over $2.1 billion. The capital will be used to expand its user base, improve its platform, and strengthen its creator community, amid a growing trend of Indian startups joining the unicorn club in 2021.

title: Three Philadelphians make Forbes' 2021 billionaire's list: Victoria Mars, Brian Roberts and Richard Hayne
summary: Forbes has released its 2021 World's Billionaires List, revealing that despite global economic turmoil caused by the pandemic, the world's wealthiest individuals have become 86% richer. Three Philadelphians, Victoria Mars, Brian Roberts, and Richard Hayne, made the list, representing major companies like Mars Inc., Comcast, and Urban Outfitters. The list grew significantly this year, adding 660 new billionaires, including a record number of women.

title: Microsoft reveals first satellite ground station at Azure data center
summary: Microsoft has installed its first satellite ground station infrastructure at an Azure data center in Quincy, Washington. This initiative, part of Azure Orbital, allows customers to directly ingest data from their satellites into Azure for processing and storage. Microsoft plans to expand its ground station network and integrate with partner ground stations, similar to AWS's existing services.

title: Atos, Dassault Systèmes, Groupe Renault, STMicroelectronics and Thales join forces to create the ‘Software République’: a new open ecosystem for intelligent and sustainable mobility
summary: Five leading companies – Atos, Dassault Systèmes, Groupe Renault, STMicroelectronics, and Thales – have partnered to establish the "Software République," an open innovation ecosystem focused on intelligent and sustainable mobility. This initiative aims to develop and market advanced software and systems utilizing AI, cybersecurity, connectivity, embedded electronics, and virtual twin technology. The collaboration seeks to ensure European sovereignty in the evolving mobility sector, address urban and regional needs, and foster innovation through an investment fund and incubator for smart mobility startups.

title: Enterprise Low-Code and Hyper-Automation: A Revolution in Digital Transformation
summary: This article discusses how enterprise low-code development and hyper-automation are revolutionizing digital transformation by empowering businesses to develop applications faster and automate critical processes. It highlights the benefits of low-code platforms such as visual development and reusability, and explains hyper-automation as a combination of BPM, RPA, and AI/ML. The article concludes by advocating for unified digital automation platforms that integrate both low-code and hyper-automation to achieve end-to-end intelligent automation.

title: Microsoft accelerates industry cloud strategy for healthcare with the acquisition of Nuance
summary: Microsoft announced its acquisition of Nuance Communications for $19.7 billion, including debt, to enhance its industry-specific cloud strategy for healthcare. This all-cash transaction will integrate Nuance's conversational AI and cloud-based ambient clinical intelligence solutions with Microsoft Cloud for Healthcare, significantly expanding Microsoft's addressable market in the healthcare provider space. Nuance CEO Mark Benjamin will continue to lead the company, reporting to Scott Guthrie, Executive Vice President of Cloud & AI at Microsoft, with the deal expected to close by the end of the calendar year and be accretive to non-GAAP earnings per share by fiscal year 2023.

title: A new Animal Crossing: New Horizons Build-A-Bear plush is coming this summer
summary: Build-A-Bear is releasing a third Animal Crossing: New Horizons-themed stuffed animal this summer, following the successful launch of Isabelle and Tom Nook plushies. The company also plans to restock Isabelle and Tom Nook soon. While the new character hasn't been officially revealed, K.K. Slider is a strong possibility.

title: Nvidia announces Omniverse Enterprise suite for real-time, photorealistic graphics design
summary: Nvidia introduced Omniverse Enterprise, a new suite designed for real-time collaborative 3D design and graphics rendering. This platform enables geographically dispersed teams to work together on complex projects, leveraging photorealistic rendering and real-time ray tracing. Key components include Omniverse Nucleus, Connectors for third-party apps, and Nvidia's own Create and View applications, with companies like BMW Group and Ericsson already using it for digital twin creation and 5G network simulation.

title: Impact Shares NAACP Minority Empowerment ETF (NACP) Stock Price, Quote, News & History
summary: This article provides detailed financial information, news, and historical data for the Impact Shares NAACP Minority Empowerment ETF (NACP). It includes key statistics like AUM, dividend, volume, and P/E ratio, along with recent news and a FAQ section covering how to buy, competitors, and dividend information. The ETF focuses on investing in large and mid-capitalization companies that empower minorities, aiming for similar risk and return characteristics to the Morningstar US Large-Mid Cap Index.

title: PlanGrid Announces Powerful New Integration Capabilities and Expanded Partner Ecosystem
summary: PlanGrid has announced PlanGrid Connect, an expansion of its API and a suite of new direct pre-built integrations, significantly bolstering its commitment to its partner ecosystem. This development allows construction teams to easily customize integrations between PlanGrid and over 100 other software solutions, eliminating the need for IT resources and preventing manual data entry errors. The new capabilities streamline information sharing, enabling real-time data access and improved collaboration across complex construction projects.

title: The future of work, phase two: what to expect
summary: Cisco leaders and customers discuss the future of work, emphasizing how cloud technology, improved communication, and hybrid models will shape a more flexible, inclusive, and secure environment. The pandemic accelerated the adoption of these changes, highlighting the importance of digital agility, employee well-being, and seamless, secure collaborative experiences for businesses, education, and healthcare.

title: NVIDIA Announces New DGX SuperPOD, the First Cloud-Native, Multi-Tenant Supercomputer, Opening World of AI to Enterprise
summary: NVIDIA has unveiled the new DGX SuperPOD, a cloud-native, multi-tenant AI supercomputer incorporating NVIDIA BlueField-2 DPUs for enhanced security and performance. This system, along with NVIDIA Base Command software, allows enterprises to securely share and operate their AI infrastructure for diverse applications like conversational AI, drug discovery, and autonomous vehicles. NVIDIA also introduced a subscription offering for the DGX Station A100, aiming to make AI development more accessible to a broader range of businesses and research institutions.

title: Network Attack Trends: Internet of Threats (November 2020-January 2021)
summary: Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 researchers analyzed network attack trends from November 2020 to January 2021, revealing that 75% of observed attacks were critical in severity. The report details top exploited vulnerabilities, newly observed exploits like CVE-2020-28188 and CVE-2020-17519, and the distribution of attack categories, with code execution accounting for 46.6% of attacks. The findings highlight the critical importance for organizations to promptly apply security patches to protect against prevalent and newly disclosed vulnerabilities.

title: Manager Question of the Month: How Active Fund Managers Cope With Index Concentration
summary: This article discusses the challenges active fund managers face due to increasing index concentration, particularly in U.S. large-cap growth benchmarks dominated by a few technology companies. It explores how managers adapt their strategies, including considering a switch from diversified to nondiversified funds, and the trade-offs involved in maintaining performance against highly concentrated indexes while adhering to SEC diversification rules. The piece highlights various approaches taken by investment firms like T. Rowe Price and Wellington Management.

title: Data processing units accelerate infrastructure performance
summary: Data processing units (DPUs) are emerging as a critical technology in data centers, offloading networking and communication tasks from CPUs to enhance infrastructure performance. This article explains how DPUs work, highlights key vendors like Fungible, Nvidia, AWS, and Nebulon, and discusses their role in software-defined infrastructure and future enterprise adoption.

title: PepsiCo leverages AI to create an intelligent monitoring system that improves Cheetos consistency
summary: PepsiCo has partnered with Microsoft Project Bonsai to develop an AI-powered monitoring system that significantly enhances the consistency of Cheetos production. This system monitors key attributes and automatically adjusts extruder settings, reducing waste and ensuring optimal product quality. The technology, which learns through reinforcement learning in simulated environments, is being piloted and explored for use across other PepsiCo products.

title: Why electric vehicles are a risky move for Polaris
summary: Polaris Inc., a major player in the off-road vehicle market, saw revenue growth in 2020 due to increased interest in powersports and outdoor activities. The company is now expanding its electric vehicle offerings, a move that some analysts view as risky. Challenges include potential performance issues with electric off-road vehicles and intense competition in the growing EV sector.

title: Dell announces long-awaited spinoff of VMware in $9B deal
summary: Dell Technologies Inc. announced the long-expected spinoff of VMware Inc., its majority-owned computing virtualization company, in a deal set to create two standalone companies. The move, aimed at simplifying capital structures and unlocking shareholder value, will see VMware distribute a cash dividend of $11.5 billion to $12 billion, with $9.3 billion to $9.7 billion going to Dell to help pay down debt. While the two companies will remain commercially linked, analysts believe the separation will boost stock prices and allow both entities to pursue independent growth opportunities.

title: Google, Adobe and Samsung top best company culture list for 2021
summary: Google, Adobe, and Samsung have topped Comparably's 2021 Best Global Company Culture list. Google led with an 85% employee approval rating, while Adobe followed closely with 96%, and Samsung was the only Asian company in the top 50. The rankings were based on anonymous employee feedback across 20 workplace culture categories, factoring in companies' handling of the pandemic and employee well-being.

title: 2020 Letter to Shareholders
summary: Jeff Bezos reflects on Amazon's growth since 1997, detailing the immense value created for shareholders, employees, third-party sellers, and customers in 2020, totaling $301 billion. He outlines new commitments for Amazon to become "Earth’s Best Employer" and "Earth’s Safest Place to Work," and discusses the company's aggressive climate change initiatives, including The Climate Pledge. Bezos concludes his final annual shareholder letter as CEO by emphasizing the importance of maintaining distinctiveness and embracing the continuous effort required for innovation and progress.

title: CoStar Group to Acquire Homes.com for $156M
summary: CoStar Group announced its intent to acquire homes-search portal Homes.com for $156 million in cash, aiming to create an agent-centric platform in contrast to competitors like Zillow. This acquisition builds on CoStar's previous purchase of Homesnap and is expected to generate $5 – $10 million in incremental revenue in the latter half of 2021. The move intensifies competition within the real estate listing portal sector, particularly against Zillow and Move.com, as tech companies vie for data and all-in-one service dominance.

title: Rackspace Technology Defines a New Category in Cloud Services
summary: Rackspace Technology (NASDAQ: RXT) has launched Rackspace Elastic Engineering, a new service model designed to help customers build and operate modern cloud environments. This new approach shifts from traditional fixed-scope managed services to providing flexible, modern, cloud-native engineering services through dedicated "Pods" of architects and engineers. Rackspace Elastic Engineering aims to support customers in their cloud-native transformations and DevOps-focused operating models across AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform.

title: Wipro clocks its best quarterly results in a decade in Q4 FY21
summary: Wipro announced its best fourth-quarter results in nearly a decade, with profit and revenue increasing by 27% and 3.4% respectively, driven by significant deal wins. The IT major forecasted a 2-4% growth for the quarter ending June, signaling a potential double-digit expansion, and won over $1.4 billion in deals including a potential $1 billion large deal. Despite rising attrition rates, Wipro plans to invest in talent, including hiring over 18,000 freshers, to sustain its growth momentum.

title: The VIG ETF: From Dividend Maintenance to Dividend Growth
summary: The VIG ETF, managed by Vanguard, focuses on companies with a history of increasing dividends over time, rather than just maintaining them. It tracks the Nasdaq US Dividend Achievers Select Index and offers exposure to large-cap equities with a low expense ratio of 0.06%. The fund includes companies that have increased dividends for at least ten consecutive years, making it suitable for long-term, dividend-focused investors.

title: Map: How Countries’ Stock Markets Stack Up on ESG Practices and Carbon Risk
summary: This article examines global stock markets' performance on ESG practices and carbon risk, based on the Morningstar Sustainability Atlas. It highlights that European countries, especially the Netherlands, lead in sustainability scores, while emerging markets generally lag. The report also identifies countries with the lowest carbon risk, such as Switzerland and the U.S., contrasting them with high-risk nations like Russia due to their energy sector exposure.

title: Zscaler Acquires Trustdome for Cloud Security Posture Management Boost -
summary: Zscaler is acquiring Trustdome to enhance its cloud security posture management (CSPM) capabilities, aiming to help MSSPs, MSPs, and customers mitigate security risks across major cloud platforms. Trustdome's Cloud Infrastructure Entitlement Management (CIEM) platform will strengthen Zscaler's existing CSPM offerings by providing granular governance over data, applications, and services in public cloud environments. This acquisition comes amidst booming demand for CSPM solutions, with market revenues projected to reach $9 billion by 2026.

title: With $27 Million In Funding, A Tiny Fintech Takes Aim At Cigna, Aetna And UnitedHealthcare
summary: Level, a New York-based fintech startup founded by Paul Aaron, has secured $27 million in Series A funding to disrupt the health insurance industry. The company aims to make insurance benefits more efficient and affordable for employees, initially focusing on dental and vision plans. Level differentiates itself by offering quick claim processing, a user-friendly app, and a unique self-funded model that allows businesses to get refunds for unused benefits, positioning itself as a challenger to established giants like Cigna, Aetna, and UnitedHealthcare.

title: Bakkt has made 3 new hires — here's who's working on the $182.5M crypto project
summary: Bakkt, Intercontinental Exchange's cryptocurrency platform, announced a massive $182.5 million funding round from partners including CMT Digital and Galaxy Digital. Despite delays in its bitcoin futures launch due to regulatory hurdles, the firm has been actively expanding its team. Key hires include Balaji Devarasetty as head of technology, Jide Laoye as technical product manager, and Peter Lee as product engineering director.

title: 10 money lessons from some of the world’s most successful people
summary: This article compiles 10 money lessons from highly successful individuals like Oprah Winfrey, Warren Buffett, and Mark Zuckerberg, offering advice on wealth management and financial success. The tips range from practical saving strategies and negotiation techniques to mindset shifts about greed, control, and the importance of investing and valuing small businesses. The overarching theme is that while money is important, understanding its dynamics and having the right perspective are crucial for achieving financial well-being and making a broader impact.

title: Praveen Sahai joins Commvault as VP - Channels, Alliances & Service Provider for APJ
summary: Commvault has announced the appointment of Praveen Sahai as Vice President - Channels, Alliances & Service Provider for Asia Pacific & Japan (APJ). In this role, Sahai will lead the growth of the APJ partner organization, focusing on strengthening relationships, driving execution excellence, and partner profitability. He brings extensive experience in SaaS, cloud computing, and data management from previous roles at Dell Technologies, Citrix, and Sun Microsystems.

title: Microsoft to invest $1 bln in Malaysia to set up data centres - Malaysian PM
summary: Microsoft Corporation announced a $1 billion investment over the next five years in Malaysia to establish its first "datacentre region" in the country. This initiative is part of a new partnership program with the Malaysian government and local companies, aiming to boost the nation's digital economy and provide digital skills training for up to a million Malaysians. The investment follows Malaysia's efforts to attract foreign direct investments after a significant decline last year.

title: DXC Technology to hire 7,000 from Indian campuses in 2021
summary: DXC Technology plans to hire 7,000 freshers from Indian campuses in 2021, a 40% increase from the previous year, due to rising demand for talent. The American IT firm, which has a 40,000-strong workforce in India, will also continue a work-from-home policy until June. This hiring drive follows the successful sale of its healthcare provider software business to Dedalus Group, strengthening its balance sheet.

title: Schlumberger Will Collaborate With Equinor for DELFI Environment Deployment, Fully Integrated With the OSDU Data Platform
summary: Schlumberger is partnering with Equinor and Microsoft to deploy the DELFI cognitive E&P environment, which will be fully integrated with the OSDU Data Platform. This collaboration aims to enhance Equinor's ability to integrate data, accelerate AI and data-driven workflows, and improve decision-making in subsurface exploration. The OSDU-enabled solution will be a key component of Equinor’s Microsoft Azure enterprise-wide data platform, OMNIA, utilizing DELFI Petrotechnical Suite and the co-developed ExplorePlan solution.

title: Zscaler expands Zero Trust from cloud to on-prem
summary: Zscaler has expanded its Zero Trust offerings with ZPA Private Service Edge, allowing organizations to deploy its cloud environment on-premise or in their own private cloud. This addresses regulatory concerns and extends Zero Trust principles by introducing Cloud Browser Isolation for secure third-party access and new APIs for automated security policy management. The company also launched a Zero Trust Academy and emphasized its ecosystem of technology partners to facilitate broader adoption and implementation of Zero Trust architectures.

title: UC, CID create innovative buzz with Great American Insurance partnership
summary: The University of Cincinnati (UC) announced a new partnership with Great American Insurance Group (GAIG), which will join the Cincinnati Innovation District (CID) and establish a workspace in UC’s 1819 Innovation Hub. This collaboration provides GAIG direct access to UC talent and resources while offering students real-world experiential learning opportunities. The partnership aims to advance innovation initiatives, foster collaboration with other corporate partners, and contribute to the region's economic growth by attracting and retaining skilled talent.

title: Hold Halliburton Stock For Long Term Gains
summary: Halliburton stock has recovered despite a subdued rig count and macroeconomic weakness, largely due to OPEC production curtailments and stable benchmark prices. The company is shifting focus to its digital business, partnering with Microsoft and Accenture, as its oilfield service segment faces challenges. While rising rig counts boosted Q4 2020 and Q1 2021 performance, future crude oil prices might see a downside as OPEC increases supply.

title: Corporate Volunteers Heed the Call of Disaster Relief
summary: Team Rubicon highlights the significant impact of corporate volunteers in disaster relief efforts, showcasing how companies like Macy's and Dow Chemical contribute both financially and through employee volunteerism. The article explains Team Rubicon's "Resilient City Strategy" to build local volunteer networks, emphasizing the role of corporate employees in these initiatives. It also details the benefits for corporations, including improved employee retention and recruitment, and how technology is used to manage and track volunteer participation.

title: Over 150,000 people in the Philippines acquire digital skills during COVID-19
summary: Microsoft announced that it has helped over 150,000 people in the Philippines acquire digital skills during the COVID-19 pandemic, as part of a global initiative that skilled over 30 million individuals. The company is extending its commitment to assist 250,000 companies globally in making skills-based hires in 2021 and establishing a skills-based economy. This effort aligns with Microsoft's "Para sa Bayan" program in the Philippines, focused on digital transformation, closing the skills gap, and enhancing employability for millions of Filipinos.

title: NVIDIA Sets AI Inference Records, Introduces A30 and A10 GPUs for Enterprise Servers
summary: NVIDIA announced its AI inference platform, featuring new A30 and A10 GPUs for mainstream servers, has achieved record-setting performance in all MLPerf benchmark categories. These GPUs offer high performance and low power consumption for enterprise AI inference, training, graphics, and traditional computing workloads, with major server manufacturers expected to integrate them soon. The platform's success highlights NVIDIA's commitment to democratizing AI, extended by its software stack and Multi-Instance GPU capability.

title: Here's how much money you'd have if you bought $1,000 worth of Netflix stock in 2011
summary: This article examines the significant return on investment for Netflix stock over the past decade. A $1,000 investment in Netflix in 2011 would have grown to over $15,000 by April 2021, far outpacing the S&P 500, Google, and Apple. Despite recent subscriber growth concerns, analysts believe Netflix is well-positioned for the long term due to its first-mover advantage and extensive content investments, even amidst increasing competition from other streaming services.

title: Xbox Series X’s FPS Boost now supports Titanfall, Battlefield 5, Star Wars Battlefront 2
summary: Microsoft has expanded its Xbox Series X’s FPS Boost feature to include 13 new Electronic Arts titles, bringing performance enhancements to popular games like Titanfall 2, Battlefield 5, and Star Wars Battlefront 2. Most of these games now support 120 frames per second on the Series X, with Sea of Solitude running at 60 fps. This addition significantly increases the total number of FPS Boost supported games, further enhancing backward compatibility on the Xbox Series X and S.

title: Get Growth With Large Cap Stability With The "VONG" ETF
summary: The article highlights the Vanguard Russell 1000 Growth Index Fund ETF Shares (VONG) as a way for investors to achieve growth with large-cap stability. VONG tracks the Russell 1000 Growth Index, focusing on large-capitalization growth stocks in the U.S., performing well with a 60% increase in the past year, driven by major tech companies. It caters to investors seeking long-term growth opportunities and capital appreciation over dividends.

title: The Glazers
summary: This article chronicles the 15-year ownership of Manchester United by the Glazer family, delving into the controversial leveraged buyout in 2005 and its impact on the club. It examines their commercial strategies, financial dealings including debt and dividends, and the persistent fan protests, while also exploring the family's approach to the business of sport, their personal involvement, and the challenges of a potential sale. The piece highlights the significant financial returns the Glazers have received and how their business model transformed Manchester United's commercial operations.

title: Ready For Take-Off: Corporate Travel Innovator Serko Straps In For Global Success
summary: New Zealand-based corporate travel software provider Serko is expanding globally through a partnership with Booking.com, leveraging Microsoft Azure for scalability and compliance. Despite challenges in the travel industry due to COVID-19, Serko anticipates significant growth as corporate travel resumes. The company's Zeno platform, now powered by Azure, is being rolled out to Booking.com for Business, targeting a vast independent SME market worldwide.

title: Get Growth With Large Cap Stability With The "VONG" ETF
summary: This article highlights the Vanguard Russell 1000 Growth Index Fund ETF Shares (VONG) as a means for investors to achieve growth with large-cap stability. VONG tracks the Russell 1000® Growth Index, focusing on large-capitalization growth stocks in the U.S. The ETF has shown significant growth over the past year, driven by prominent technology companies.

title: Cybersecurity startup Deep Instinct raises $100 million in funding round
summary: Deep Instinct, an Israeli cybersecurity firm, successfully raised $100 million in Series D funding, bringing its total funding to date to $200 million. The company leverages deep learning algorithms to predict and prevent cyberattacks and plans to use the new capital to expand its market capabilities and further develop its AI platform into cloud, network, and storage security. The funding round was led by BlackRock, with participation from Untitled Investments and existing investors.

title: Coronavirus vaccine passports: everything you need to know
summary: The article discusses the global debate around COVID-19 vaccine passports, detailing their purpose, current usage in various countries, and the concerns they raise. These digital tools aim to certify immunity through vaccination, negative tests, or recovery, helping ease lockdowns and reopen economies. However, critics highlight issues regarding privacy, equity, and the scientific validity of immunity.

title: Billionaire Beat: Zscaler Entrepreneur Jay Chaudhry Has Built A Cloud Security Powerhouse
summary: Jay Chaudhry, founder and CEO of Zscaler, has become a self-made billionaire by building a leading cloud security company. Originating from humble beginnings in India, Chaudhry has a net worth of $11 billion and is motivated by securing the cloud and Internet. Zscaler experienced massive growth in 2020 due to the increased necessity for remote work cybersecurity amidst the pandemic, with its stock rising nearly 300%.

title: Evercore joins as advisor for S.Korea’s Hanon Systems stake sale
summary: Evercore Inc. is partnering with Morgan Stanley to co-manage the sale of a majority stake in Hanon Systems Corp., a South Korean auto parts supplier. The sellers aim to gain at least 8 trillion won ($7.2 billion) from the sale, which includes holdings from Hahn & Co. and potentially Hankook Tire & Technology Co. Potential bidders like LG Electronics Inc. and Volkswagen are being considered.

title: Nature as a building block for Microsoft’s new Silicon Valley Campus
summary: Microsoft's new Silicon Valley campus in Mountain View, California, is designed as an ecologically integrated site, earning it a spot on the COTE Top Ten list for its sustainable features. The campus incorporates water reuse, clean energy production, carbon reduction, and native ecology restoration. Key elements include an extensive solar panel system, an integrated water management system for net-zero non-potable water, and the use of Cross Laminated Timber to reduce its carbon footprint.

title: Semiconductor maker Skyworks to acquire Silicon Laboratories' infrastructure and automotive business for $2.75bn
summary: Skyworks Solutions plans to acquire Silicon Laboratories' infrastructure and automotive business for $2.75 billion to expand into new markets like industrial, 5G wireless infrastructure, and data centers. This acquisition will help Skyworks diversify its revenue and leverage its global sales channels while Silicon Labs' team brings decades of innovation. The move also positions Skyworks in the automotive market amid a global semiconductor shortage impacting car manufacturers.

title: John Deere Addresses the Ongoing Risks of Living in a Digital World
summary: John Deere is actively addressing cybersecurity and data privacy concerns in the increasingly digitized agricultural sector. The company's vice president of data applications and analytics, Lane Arthur, discusses their commitment to safeguarding farmer data, including a full-time security team, regular software security checkpoints, and collaboration with industry partners to promote transparency and secure data transfer. Farmers are encouraged to review their data-sharing settings within the John Deere Operations Center.

title: Why Dow Chemical Is Embracing a Hybrid Cloud Environment
summary: Dow Chemical, a company with over a century of business, is transitioning to a hybrid cloud environment, leveraging partners like IBM and Microsoft Azure. The move is driven by a need for increased agility, speed to market, and cost optimization, addressing technical debt from its centralized, mainframe-centric IT systems. This migration involves challenges such as maintaining security, performance, and cost efficiency, while also requiring extensive training and upskilling for its IT staff to manage both on-premises and cloud infrastructures.

title: Xbox Game Pass - Is Microsoft on track to be the 'Netflix of Games'?
summary: This article analyzes whether Xbox Game Pass is on track to become the "Netflix of Games" by comparing its growth and strategy to Netflix's journey. It examines Game Pass's content library, quality, developer partnerships, international appeal, and technological advancements like cloud gaming. The author concludes that while Game Pass is still in its early stages and has areas to improve, its rapid growth and strategic direction suggest it is well-positioned for significant success, mirroring Netflix's disruptive impact on its industry.

title: ‘That’s crazy!’: Tesla CEO Musk gives carbon removal $100m boost
summary: Elon Musk has launched a $100 million prize competition to encourage the development of new carbon capture technologies. The initiative aims to address the pressing need for scalable and affordable methods to remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and oceans, thereby combating global warming. This four-year challenge, described as the largest incentive prize in history, seeks viable solutions capable of removing 1,000 tonnes of CO2 annually with long-term sequestration.

title: Fintech boosted by Quantum Computing? Ally joins Microsoft Quantum Azure to explore use cases
summary: Ally, a financial company, is collaborating with Microsoft's Azure Quantum program to explore how quantum-inspired algorithms can solve optimization problems in fintech, such as financial risk assessment. This partnership aims to leverage cloud-based quantum computing without requiring Ally to invest in specialized hardware. The initiative highlights a growing trend in exploring quantum computing's potential for complex calculations and machine learning in finance.

title: The FBI is breaking into corporate computers to remove malicious code – smart cyber defense or government overreach?
summary: The FBI has begun accessing private corporate computers, without owner consent, to remove malicious code installed by hackers, particularly affecting Microsoft Exchange servers. This action, permitted by a U.S. District Court, is part of a broader "active defense" cybersecurity strategy but raises significant legal and ethical questions about government overreach, property rights, and the extent of judicial power in cybersecurity regulation, especially under the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act and Rule 41 of the Federal Rules of Criminal Procedure. The unprecedented move highlights discussions about market failure in cybersecurity and the evolving role of the government in protecting critical infrastructure.

title: Wonbang Tech: S.Korea’s leading chip clean room company
summary: Wonbang Tech is a leading South Korean company specializing in the construction of industrial "dry rooms" and "clean rooms" for the semiconductor, electronic display, and battery industries. They serve major companies like Samsung, SK Hynix, and LG, and are known for their technical expertise in humidity and temperature control. The company is diversifying into bio clean rooms for pharmaceuticals and Internet Data Centers to stabilize its business beyond the cyclical semiconductor and battery industries.

title: How managed multi-cloud services help create an industrialized approach
summary: This article discusses how managed multi-cloud services enable enterprises to adopt an industrialized approach to IT, ensuring agility and effective management of both cloud and non-cloud resources. It highlights how these services help meet business imperatives, foster innovation through CoEs and advanced technologies, and optimize IT consumption. Wipro's BoundaryLess Enterprise (BLE) platform is presented as a solution for accelerating cloud transformation and aligning business objectives with IT resource consumption.

title: First Person: Litigator David Boies On Antitrust, Tech And The Government V. Microsoft
summary: Litigator David Boies discusses his experience representing the government in the landmark antitrust case against Microsoft in the late 1990s. He explains how Microsoft's monopolistic practices were challenged and reflects on the lessons learned from that case, particularly concerning the applicability of antitrust laws to technology companies. Boies also touches on the challenges of applying these regulations to modern tech giants like Amazon, emphasizing the need for fact-specific analysis.

title: Intel vs Advanced Micro Devices (AMD)
summary: This article analyzes the long-standing rivalry between Intel and AMD, comparing their historical market dominance, recent performance, financial health, and future outlook. It highlights AMD's recent surge due to TSMC's advanced chip manufacturing, challenging Intel's traditional leadership. The author concludes by positioning AMD as a growth play and Intel as a value play, considering potential comebacks and ongoing industry challenges like chip shortages.

title: ICE Mortgage Technology’s Latest Origination Insight Report Shows Significant Reduction in Time to Close
summary: A new report from ICE Mortgage Technology shows a significant reduction in the time it takes to close all loan types, decreasing from 58 days in January 2021 to 52 days in March 2021. This improvement is attributed to lenders adopting digital mortgage tools. The report also highlights an increase in closing rates and a shift towards purchase loans as refinance volumes remain high.

title: Lovesac builds a customer experience platform for life with Adobe Commerce
summary: Lovesac, recognized as the fastest-growing furniture retailer, has partnered with Adobe Commerce to build a flexible and scalable customer experience platform. This move supports their "designed for life" philosophy and sustainable products, enabling them to adapt to changing customer behaviors and thrive, especially during the COVID-19 pandemic. The partnership has led to double-digit growth in conversion rates and average order values and positions Lovesac for continuous innovation in its online presence.

title: Looking for an ETF to Hold for the Long-Term?
summary: The article suggests the Schwab U.S. Large-Cap Growth ETF (SCHG) as a long-term investment option, highlighting its strong performance and holdings in major growth companies. It emphasizes the potential for significant long-term returns through consistent investing in such ETFs, despite the allure of instant gratification.

title: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) 4th Earnings: What to Expect
summary: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) is set to report its first-quarter fiscal 2021 earnings, with expectations rising due to strong performance from rival Intel and increasing chip demand. Analysts predict earnings of 44 cents per share on $3.21 billion in revenue for the quarter, largely driven by gains in datacenter revenue and PC demand, where AMD has been taking market share from Intel. The company's gross margin growth and the recent Xilinx acquisition are also expected to contribute to its continued momentum.

title: These 3 ETFs Sit Atop the Invesco Fund Flows Leaderboard
summary: This article highlights the top three Invesco ETFs by year-to-date fund flows as of April 2021. The ETFs include the Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF (RSP), the Invesco PureBeta MSCI USA ETF (PBUS), and the Invesco Senior Loan ETF (BKLN). Each ETF offers a distinct strategy, ranging from equal-weighting and pure beta exposure to senior loan investments.

title: Campbell Soup Company transforms IT and boosts supply chain visibility with a single global SAP HANA environment on Azure
summary: Campbell Soup Company migrated its SAP environments to SAP HANA on Microsoft Azure to improve reliability, availability, and scalability, especially after acquiring Snyder’s-Lance. This transformation has significantly reduced downtime, made manufacturing more resilient, and provided deeper insights into its supply chain, supported by a strategic partnership with Microsoft and Khoj Information Technology. The company achieved substantial performance improvements and is now better positioned for future growth and acquisitions.

title: 8x8 pushes work collaboration through a browser
summary: 8x8 has expanded its Work for Web platform and improved its Meet video conferencing software, enabling more users to collaborate through web browsers instead of dedicated apps. This move aims to support the hybrid workplace by allowing employees to use various devices and offers several benefits for IT organizations by reducing app downloads and support. The updates also include new features like customizable backgrounds, call silencing, and inline replies in chat.

title: Cyber Security for Financial Institutions
summary: The financial sector is undergoing modernization with new technologies, creating additional attack surfaces and making financial institutions prime targets for cyber attacks. Check Point Software's Infinity Platform offers AI-powered, cloud-delivered comprehensive protection, regulatory compliance, operational efficiency, and advanced threat prevention to safeguard financial institutions, their data, and customer trust. The platform aims to combat the rising cost of data breaches and the increasing number of cyber attacks faced by the industry.

title: Microsoft Beats Wall Street’s Expectations With Strong Q3 Earnings
summary: Microsoft announced strong third-quarter earnings for fiscal 2021, surpassing Wall Street expectations with $41.7 billion in revenue and $2.03 diluted EPS. Key growth drivers included Office 365, Dynamics 365, Microsoft Teams, and Xbox sales, though slower growth in Azure led to a 3% drop in shares after hours. Despite the after-hours dip, the company's stock has performed well year-to-date and over the past 12 months.

title: Highwoods Properties Inc (HIW) Q1 2021 Earnings Call Transcript
summary: Highwoods Properties Inc. (HIW) reported Q1 2021 FFO of $0.91 per share and increased its full-year FFO outlook, driven by improved leasing activity and strong performance in its Sunbelt markets. The company also announced plans to acquire a portfolio of office assets from Preferred Apartment Communities for $769 million, funded by selling $500-600 million in non-core assets. Executives highlighted rising office utilization rates, significant job growth announcements in their key markets like Raleigh and Nashville, and continued optimism for long-term growth.

title: Microsoft plans to take a smaller cut from developers in its games store. (Published 2021)
summary: Microsoft announced that it will decrease the revenue cut it takes from independent developers publishing PC games on its online store, starting in August. The fee will drop from 30 percent to 12 percent, allowing developers to keep 88 percent of their revenue. This move aims to make Microsoft's store more competitive with platforms like Steam and Epic Games, and comes amid increased scrutiny over app store fees faced by companies like Apple and Google.

title: Microsoft Store announces that 'PC game sales commission will be reduced from 30% to 12%', moving to break Steam's stronghold
summary: Microsoft is reducing its sales commission for PC games sold on the Microsoft Store from 30% to 12%, effective August 1, 2021, to encourage game publishers and developers. This move aims to compete with platforms like Steam, which traditionally charges a 30% commission, and aligns with Epic Games' commission structure. The change applies only to PC games and is part of Microsoft's broader strategy to invest in the PC gaming ecosystem and improve the Microsoft Store experience.

title: A Conservative ETF That Boycotts Liberal Companies Is Beating the S&P 500
summary: The American Conservative Values ETF ($ACVF), which boycotts companies supporting a "liberal agenda," has outperformed the S&P 500 since President Biden took office, gaining 9.1% compared to the S&P 500's 8.7%. The fund's founder, Bill Flaig, believes politically active companies negatively impact shareholder returns and aims to provide conservative investors with an option that aligns with their values. While acknowledging the subjectivity in defining "hostile" companies, the fund seeks to balance advocacy with predictable large-cap performance.

title: Building a Resilient E-Commerce Business with Arrow Electronics
summary: This article discusses how Arrow Electronics, a global distributor, is building a resilient e-commerce business in response to market disruptions and the impact of COVID-19. It details how the company adopted SAP Commerce Cloud and restructured operations to improve customer experience and achieve business agility through digital transformation. The article highlights the importance of adapting to B2B buyer demands and leveraging technology to overcome supply chain challenges.

title: With Everything Up Right Now, Where are the Value Buying Opportunities?
summary: This article by Frank Holmes discusses the current economic climate where most asset classes are experiencing significant price appreciation due to monetary and fiscal stimulus. It highlights areas of inflation, such as lumber, homes, cars, and commodities, and then pinpoints gold and gold miners as potential value buying opportunities, given their underperformance compared to other commodities. The article also touches on the rising crypto market and issues faced by crypto miners, as well as broader market trends, energy, and emerging markets.

title: Preventing Ransomware Exposures from Remote Desk Protocol
summary: This article discusses the risks of ransomware attacks through Remote Desk Protocol (RDP) and Server Message Block (SMB), common tools for remote work. It explains how cybercriminals exploit exposed ports to scan for vulnerabilities, gain access, disable security, and deploy ransomware. The article then provides seven best practices to strengthen RDP security, including closing RDP connections, establishing a VPN, elevating authentication protocols, implementing login attempt limits, utilizing adequate security software, restricting employee access, and having a cyber incident response plan.

title: HRD Corp And Microsoft Aligns Program For 300,000 Professionals Needed For Data Centre
summary: HRD Corp and Microsoft are collaborating to train 300,000 Malaysian professionals for the digital economy over the next three years, supporting Microsoft's new regional data center investment and the MyDigital blueprint. This partnership will utilize Microsoft's digital skilling content in AI, IoT, and digital business, with HRD Corp facilitating training and placement opportunities. The initiative aims to enhance Malaysian employability and is projected to generate significant new revenues for the country.

title: SP Funds S&P 500 Sharia Industry Exclusions ETF (SPUS) holdings
summary: This article details the holdings and key characteristics of the SP Funds S&P 500 Sharia Industry Exclusions ETF (SPUS). The fund invests in constituents of the S&P 500 Shariah Index, excluding specific sub-industries like Aerospace & Defense and Financial Exchanges.

title: Honeywell Just Dumped the New York Stock Exchange for the Nasdaq. Here’s Why.
summary: Honeywell International is moving its stock listing from the New York Stock Exchange to Nasdaq. This unexpected decision is primarily driven by perception, but it also carries potential stock implications for investors to consider. The company has also established a new software unit, led by a former Microsoft executive.

title: 2021 Tech Titans
summary: This article highlights the 2021 Tech Titans in Washington D.C.'s digital economy, recognizing over 170 influential leaders, innovators, and officials who demonstrated resilience and growth despite the pandemic. It showcases entrepreneurs who launched new companies, secured significant funding, and adapted their businesses, along with key figures in finance, cybersecurity, government, and policy. The piece also acknowledges leaders in the satellite, telecommunications, and defense industries who are shaping the region's tech landscape.

title: CoStar To Employees: Come Back To The Office And Get A Tesla
summary: CoStar is incentivizing its vaccinated employees to return to the office with a variety of prizes, including a new Tesla, $10,000 cash, and an all-expenses-paid trip to Barbados. This initiative, launched alongside a company-wide vaccine rollout, aims to boost office occupancy, which has risen from 4 percent to 20 percent since the program began. CEO Andrew Florance stated that these creative incentives are part of an ongoing effort to adjust to new workplace realities post-pandemic, as other companies also explore various strategies to encourage office returns.

title: Intapp enters the document management space with acquisition of Repstor
summary: Intapp has acquired Repstor, a Belfast-headquartered cloud content management systems provider, expanding its platform into fee-earner work product and document management. This acquisition will enable Intapp to better cater to law firms leveraging Microsoft 365, particularly Teams, for client matter management and file sharing. The move positions Intapp as a significant competitor in the document management world, offering an alternative to existing solutions like iManage and NetDocuments.

title: 3 Clicks to $4,000 a Month in Dividend Income
summary: This article proposes that Closed-End Funds (CEFs) offer a superior alternative to ETFs for generating significant retirement income, highlighting their higher dividend yields. It outlines a portfolio of three specific CEFs—Nuveen NASDAQ 100 Dynamic Overwrite Fund (QQQX), Guggenheim Strategic Opportunities Fund (GOF), and PIMCO Corporate & Income Opportunities Fund (PTY)—that collectively provide an 8.5% payout and strong diversification. The author argues that CEFs enable investors to achieve a substantial passive income stream with a much smaller initial investment compared to traditional S&P 500 dividend ETFs, ultimately leading to financial independence faster.

title: Microsoft will permanently remove Flash from Windows PCs by July 2021
summary: Microsoft announced its plan to permanently remove Adobe Flash Player from Windows PCs by July 2021, addressing a significant security risk left by Flash's end-of-life status. This removal process, which began with optional updates in September 2020 and expanded to silent deployments in February 2021, aims to eliminate the defunct software that no longer receives updates and is vulnerable to exploitation. The move is largely uncontroversial given that Adobe itself embedded a "time bomb" rendering Flash unusable after January 2021, making its removal a secure and practical solution.

title: Vancouver, Seattle, Portland mega-region concept lives on
summary: The concept of a Cascadia mega-region, connecting Vancouver, Seattle, and Portland via high-speed rail, is gaining momentum as a way to boost economic growth and create smart density. While developers recognize the strong fundamentals of cities like Seattle, particularly for its tech sector and ease of doing business, there are questions about the synergistic benefits for Vancouver and the significant cost of the proposed $42 billion rail link. The initiative is seen by many as crucial for regional competitiveness, though some express skepticism about the depth of commitment from U.S. tech companies and the ability to navigate different political frameworks.

title: Epic Games CEO cites Apple’s ‘total control’ over iPhones at first day of antitrust trial
summary: Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney testified on the first day of the antitrust trial against Apple, stating his deliberate violation of Apple's App Store rules to spotlight the company's "total control" over software on iPhones. The lawsuit challenges Apple's mandatory App Store distribution and in-app purchase system, which charges up to 30% commissions. Epic argues Apple's practices stifle competition, while Apple contends its rules ensure user safety and a thriving market for developers.

title: McGraw Hill Acquires Triad Interactive, Developer of SIMnet, an Online Training Platform for Microsoft Office
summary: McGraw Hill has acquired Triad Interactive, the developer of SIMnet, an online training platform for Microsoft Office used in undergraduate computer and IT courses. This acquisition follows a two-decade partnership where Triad developed and updated SIMnet, and McGraw Hill marketed and distributed it. The deal aims to enhance SIMnet, improve customer support, and expand its reach to a larger audience, with Triad's founders joining McGraw Hill in consulting roles.

title: How wearable technology is transforming wellbeing in the workplace
summary: Wearable technology, ranging from smartwatches to specialized helmets and goggles, is increasingly being adopted in workplaces to enhance employee wellbeing and performance. This article explores the growing market for wearables, strategic shifts in their application, and the challenges associated with their implementation in creating smarter workplaces. The integration of these devices aims to help employees stay healthier and more productive.

title: Microsoft’s new partnership with the Nigerian government aims to upskill 5 million Nigerians
summary: Microsoft has partnered with the Nigerian Federal Government to accelerate the country’s digital economy, aiming to upskill five million people and create over 27,000 digital jobs within three years. This collaboration focuses on connectivity, skilling, and digital transformation, aligning with Nigeria's economic sustainable plan. Additionally, Microsoft will use AI tools to help protect Nigeria’s cultural heritage, including its indigenous languages.

title: Bill Gates Gives $1.8 Billion in Stocks to Melinda on Day Divorce Filed
summary: Bill Gates transferred approximately $1.8 billion worth of stock in two companies to Melinda Gates on the same day she filed for divorce. This major transaction, involving shares in Canadian National Railway Co. and AutoNation Inc., suggests that the couple had already worked out parts of their property settlement prior to the public announcement of their divorce. The divorce filing indicated no prenup, and the stock transfer is the initial reveal of their asset division.

title: Azure vs Google Cloud: How They Compare
summary: This article provides a detailed comparison between Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud Platform, covering their market position, pricing models, and specific services for storage, compute, and networking. It highlights their strengths and weaknesses, such as Azure's comprehensive solutions and Google Cloud's competitive pricing and strong container support. The piece aims to help users understand which cloud provider might be a better fit based on their specific needs and existing infrastructure.

title: Melinda Gates becomes CN Rail’s sixth biggest shareholder after stock transfer following divorce announcement
summary: Following the announcement of their divorce, Bill Gates' Cascade Investment LLC transferred 14 million shares of Canadian National Railway Co., valued at approximately $1.8-billion, to Melinda Gates. This transfer makes Melinda Gates the sixth-biggest shareholder in CN Rail. Cascade Investment remains CN's largest shareholder, and the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation also holds a significant stake in the railway.

title: Intermedia Cloud Communications Announces New Microsoft Teams Integrations to Enhance Business Communications
summary: Intermedia Cloud Communications has announced two new integrations of its Intermedia Unite® solution with Microsoft Teams to enhance business communications. These packages add enterprise-grade business phone features, contact center, and business SMS capabilities to Microsoft Teams, catering to businesses already using Teams for collaboration or looking for a fully integrated cloud communications platform. Intermedia aims to provide a more versatile, complete, and reliable communications experience for organizations transitioning to hybrid work models.

title: How Data-Sharing Is Helping to Power a Global CPG Company
summary: The Kraft Heinz Company transformed its data infrastructure by moving from an on-premises Hadoop system to the Snowflake Data Cloud, enhancing its ability to innovate and respond to market changes. This digital transformation, driven by scalability, agility, and cloud-agnosticism, enables Kraft Heinz to easily access third-party data sets, like COVID-19 data from Johns Hopkins University, for predictive modeling and supply chain optimization. The company is also fostering a data-driven culture by recruiting talent and implementing learning programs, anticipating a future where data sharing among organizations is seamless and secure.

title: II-VI optimistic as Apple backs further VCSEL expansion and development
summary: II-VI reported a 25% annual increase in revenues, reaching $783 million for the quarter ending March 31, and expressed optimism for the future, particularly regarding its pending merger with Coherent. The company also announced that Apple has pledged an additional $410 million from its "Advanced Manufacturing Fund" to support II-VI's production of VCSELs, which are critical for Apple's Face ID and lidar scanner technologies. Despite near-term caution due to a global electronic components shortage, II-VI anticipates continued growth driven by megatrends and the expanded capabilities from the Coherent acquisition.

title: HRD Corp and Microsoft to train and place 300,000 Malaysian digital professionals in three years
summary: HRD Corp and Microsoft Malaysia have partnered to train and place 300,000 Malaysian digital professionals over the next three years, supporting the nation's digital workforce growth and MyDigital aspirations. This initiative involves Microsoft sharing digital skilling content and HRD Corp facilitating training and placement opportunities. The collaboration is a key component of the "Bersama Malaysia" initiative, aiming to empower every person and organization in Malaysia to thrive in the digital economy.

title: Anto Tossounian, Brian Fogg: ServiceNow-GDIT Partnership Enables Government to Modernize Digital Experience
summary: Anto Tossounian of ServiceNow and Brian Fogg of General Dynamics Information Technology (GDIT) discussed their partnership to help government agencies modernize digital services and enhance customer experience. Their collaboration provides cloud-based managed services for government enterprises, focusing on automating workflows for IT, HR, and contact centers. The partnership also enabled ServiceNow to achieve Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program High and DoD Impact Level 5 authorization for its services on Microsoft Azure.

title: Apple Has Hired Cisco's Stella Low As Its Head Of PR
summary: Apple has hired Stella Low, former communications chief at Cisco, as its new vice president of worldwide corporate communications. She will report directly to Apple CEO Tim Cook and fills a role that has been vacant for nearly two years. Low's appointment comes at a critical time for Apple, as the company faces high-profile legal battles, geopolitical tensions, and prepares for significant product launches.

title: Help With Vaccination Push Comes From Unexpected Businesses (Published 2021)
summary: Major companies like Microsoft, Starbucks, and Amazon are assisting the government's COVID-19 vaccination efforts by offering logistical support, physical locations, and operational expertise. These companies, despite not being directly in healthcare, are leveraging their vast resources, national footprints, and distribution networks to help with the rollout. This private sector involvement aims to boost the vaccination drive and could enhance the companies' public image and bottom line.

title: Microsoft pulls Windows 10 AMD driver causing PCs not to boot
summary: Microsoft has withdrawn an AMD driver from Windows Update after reports that it caused Windows 10 PCs to fail to boot, displaying an "INACCESSIBLE BOOT DEVICE" error. The problematic driver, 'Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. - SCSIAdapter - 9.3.0.221', was rolled out to incompatible hardware after an initial testing phase, affecting primarily owners of Gigabyte X570 motherboards. Many users were able to fix the issue through Automatic Startup Repair, while others required more complex solutions.

title: AMD SCSIAdapter 9.3.0.221 update is crashing Windows 10 PCs
