The initiative builds upon Morgan Stanley’s existing in-house start-up accelerator and seeks to partner with additional corporate organizations sharing similar strategic interests.

title: A supply-chain breach: Taking over an Atlassian account
summary: Check Point Research (CPR) uncovered and responsibly disclosed chained vulnerabilities in Atlassian's platform that could lead to full account takeover. These vulnerabilities, including XSS, CSRF, and Cookie Fixation, allowed attackers to bypass security measures like SameSite "Strict" cookies and HttpOnly cookies. The attack chain enabled taking over accounts on various Atlassian subdomains such as training.atlassian.com and jira.atlassian.com, posing significant risks to data collaboration and information sharing for Atlassian's millions of users.

title: Combating Lateral Movement and the Rise of Ransomware
summary: The article discusses the significant surge in ransomware attacks, exacerbated by the shift to virtual work environments during the pandemic, and how these attacks now pose a national security risk. It details the five phases of a ransomware attack, emphasizing lateral movement as a critical stage where threat actors are most vulnerable to detection. The piece concludes by outlining three core elements to combat lateral movement: purpose-built Managed Detection & Response (MDR) platforms, proactive threat hunting by experienced analysts, and strict cybersecurity hygiene and IT best practices.

Heise also serves on the board of directors for Essent Guaranty.

summary: Intel and Microsoft are collaborating to enhance the Windows 11 experience, particularly for the over 75% of Windows PCs powered by Intel processors. This partnership aims to deliver unmatched performance, compatibility, and user experiences by integrating Intel's hardware advancements with Microsoft's software.

summary: Broadcom, MediaTek, and Marvell have publicly expressed their support for Nvidia's $40 billion acquisition of Arm, despite scrutiny from antitrust regulators and concerns from rivals like Qualcomm, Google, and Microsoft. These chip heavyweights cite assurances from Nvidia regarding increased investment in Arm's technology and continued fair access for the industry. The support comes as Nvidia and Arm CEOs argue the deal is necessary to meet growing demand and accelerate technological roadmaps in the semiconductor industry amidst a global chip shortage.

title: How Salesforce, Amazon, Google measure climate impact
summary: This article discusses how companies like Salesforce, Amazon, and Google are measuring their climate impact and the challenges involved. The piece also emphasizes the importance of internal communication, incentives, and policymaker involvement in achieving climate goals.

summary: NVIDIA has enhanced its HGX AI supercomputing platform with new technologies designed to accelerate industrial AI and High-Performance Computing (HPC). title: Antitrust and Platform Monopoly

The author proposes remedies beyond breaking up companies, such as restructuring management, requiring interoperability, or mandating information pooling to foster competition and leverage network effects, while also noting that existing merger enforcement tools are inadequate for platform acquisitions of nascent firms.

HP also expanded its M-Series monitors with the M24fwa and M27fwa FHD monitors, which are Eyesafe certified and made with recycled materials.

title: AT&T to run its mobility network on Microsoft’s Azure for Operators cloud, delivering cost-efficient 5G services at scale
summary: AT&T is moving its 5G mobile network to Microsoft's Azure for Operators cloud, leveraging Microsoft Azure technologies for managing its mobile network traffic, starting with its 5G core. This strategic alliance aims to increase AT&T's productivity and cost efficiency while giving Microsoft access to AT&T's Network Cloud platform technology and engineering talent to enhance its Azure for Operators offering. The collaboration is expected to help operators worldwide deliver reliable and cost-effective 5G services and accelerate the transition of network workloads to the cloud.

title: Best Pride Month Marketing Campaigns
summary: This article examines the challenges and successes of Pride Month marketing campaigns, emphasizing the importance of authenticity. It showcases several brands like Lego, H&M, Havaianas, Sainsbury's, Vindicia, Microsoft, and Quint Media, highlighting their strategies for effective and genuine engagement with the LGBTQIA+ community. The piece concludes by noting the growing market influence of the LGBTQ+ community and advocating for year-round support and mindful marketing.

title: HPE buys Israeli cloud data co Zerto for $374m
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) has announced its acquisition of Israeli cloud data management and protection company Zerto for $374 million in cash. Zerto's technology, which includes disaster recovery, backup, and data mobility, will be integrated into HPE's GreenLake cloud data services. This acquisition is expected to contribute over $130 million in run-rate revenue to HPE.

title: HPE To Acquire Zerto For $374M To Boost GreenLake, Storage
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise is acquiring cloud data management and storage protection specialist Zerto for $374 million to enhance its HPE GreenLake cloud data services. This acquisition is expected to add over $130 million in run-rate revenue and will strengthen HPE's shift towards a cloud-native, software-defined data services business. Zerto's technology offers continuous data protection, disaster recovery, backup, and data mobility across various environments, and will be integrated into HPE GreenLake's as-a-service portfolio.

title: Euro Tax Flash from KPMG's EU Tax Centre
summary: KPMG's Euro Tax Flash reports on the historic agreement reached by 130 countries in the OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework on BEPS 2.0, aiming to reform international tax rules with a two-pillar approach. Pillar One reallocates taxing rights for large companies to market countries, while Pillar Two establishes a global minimum tax rate of at least 15%. The article also discusses potential EU implementation challenges and notes that some countries, like Ireland, have reservations about certain aspects of the agreement.
